\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.1}
\begin{prop}[{Order compatible with addition and multiplication on Z}]\label{thm:rr-lt-add}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{rr-lt-add}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall x, y, u, v \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (((x < y) \wedge (u \leq v)) \Rightarrow ((x + u) < (y + v))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{rr-mul-le-right}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((a \leq b) \Rightarrow ((0 \leq c) \Rightarrow ((a \cdot c) \leq (b \cdot c)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{rr-mul-pos}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad ((0 < a) \Rightarrow ((0 < b) \Rightarrow (0 < (a \cdot b)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (8 steps; 3 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ineq 2 arguments)}}}}
%

%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The additive half is rr-lt-add, stated over RR (x $<$ y and u $<$= v implies x + u $<$ y + v), not over ZZ; ZZ inherits it through zz-in-rr. The multiplicative half, a $<$ b and c in NN implies a * c $<$ b * c, is NOT stated anywhere: rr-mul-le-right is the NON-STRICT form (a $<$= b and 0 $<$= c implies a * c $<$= b * c) and rr-mul-pos gives only 0 $<$ a and 0 $<$ b implies 0 $<$ a * b. There is also no ZZ-specific order lemma of either shape; the notes derive both from the definition b - a in N, which the library does not use.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.3}
\begin{prop}[{1 is the least natural number}]\label{thm:nn-one-le-succ}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{nn-one-le-succ}}
\vnbstmt{\forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; (1 \leq (n + 1))}
\vnbpart{\texttt{zz-discrete}}
\vnbstmt{\forall \alpha \in \mathbb{Z}.\; ((0 < \alpha) \Rightarrow (1 \leq \alpha))}
\vnbpart{\texttt{nn-pos-is-succ}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad ((1 \leq n) \Rightarrow \exists q \in \mathbb{N}.\; (n = (q + 1))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\begin{prop}[{Uniqueness of the least upper bound}]\label{thm:calculus-1.9}
%
\textit{For any set S, least upper bounds a, a' for S are identical.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Nothing states that two least upper bounds of a subset of RR coincide. The library takes sup as a total functoid governed by the three axioms rr-sup-in, rr-sup-upper, rr-sup-least (all three stamped asserted, warrant: reference), so uniqueness is built into the notation rather than proved. The nearest statements are esup-unique, which is the same claim for the EXTENDED nonnegative reals rr-pos-star with bounds quantified over rr-pos-star, and the axiom rr-leq-antisymmetric from which the notes' one-line proof would run.

\begin{prop}[{The nested interval property}]\label{thm:rr-nested-intervals}
%

The extended line exists only as the membership predicate rr-star-membership (x in RR-STAR iff x in RR or x = POS-INF or x = NEG-INF) with the two order axioms pos-inf-upper-bound and neg-inf-lower-bound; there is no order-isomorphism vocabulary for it and no extension of the map to the closed interval [-1, 1].

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.3}
\begin{prop}[{Higher derivatives of x\textasciicircum{}n}]\label{thm:nth-deriv-monomial}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{nth-deriv-monomial}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n, \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; \operatorname{power}(x, n)), \mathit{tck}) \simeq (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; ((\operatorname{factorial}(n) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\operatorname{nn\text{-}minus}(n, \mathit{tck})))) \cdot \operatorname{power}(x, \operatorname{nn\text{-}minus}(n, \mathit{tck}))))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{nth-deriv-monomial-vanish}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n, \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad (n < \mathit{tck}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; \operatorname{power}(x, n)), \mathit{tck}) \simeq (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; 0)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.4}
\begin{prop}[{Differentiability implies continuity}]\label{thm:diff-implies-continuous}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-implies-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, a, l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, a) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-implies-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k, u, f, a, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, f, a, l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(\operatorname{nf\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(k), u), \operatorname{nf\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(k), f, a) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.5}
\begin{prop}[{Derivative of a sum}]\label{thm:deriv-sum}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{deriv-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, a, l, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, a, l) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(g, a, m) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (f(x) + g(x))), a, (l + m)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2m}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{d2x} \in u.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{add}(k)(\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2x}), \operatorname{d2g}(\mathit{d2x}))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{d2a}, \operatorname{add}(k)(\mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.6}
\begin{prop}[{Derivative of a product}]\label{thm:deriv-product}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{deriv-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, a, l, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, a, l) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(g, a, m) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (f(x) \cdot g(x))), a, ((l \cdot g(a)) + (f(a) \cdot m))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2m}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{d2x} \in u.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mul}(k)(\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2x}), \operatorname{d2g}(\mathit{d2x}))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{d2a}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{add}(k)(\operatorname{mul}(k)(\mathit{d2l}, \operatorname{d2g}(\mathit{d2a})), \operatorname{mul}(k)(\mathit{d2m}, \operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2a})))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The notes state the ONE-SIDED form; the library has only the two-sided derivative (D2). deriv-product requires f and g total on RR (D1). diff-on-product is the same law for is-diff-on over a normed field k with U open. Note the notes give no hypothesis on g beyond right differentiability at x, and neither does the library.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.8}
\begin{prop}[{Chain Rule}]\label{thm:has-deriv-at-chain}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{has-deriv-at-chain}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{crr}. \\ \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{crr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f, g, h, \mathit{crx}, \mathit{crl}, \mathit{crm}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{restrict}(h, \operatorname{ooint}((\mathit{crx} - \mathit{crr}), (\mathit{crx} + \mathit{crr}))) \\ \quad \quad \quad \in\; (\operatorname{ooint}((\mathit{crx} - \mathit{crr}), (\mathit{crx} + \mathit{crr})) \to \mathbb{R}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{cry} \in \operatorname{ooint}((\mathit{crx} - \mathit{crr}), (\mathit{crx} + \mathit{crr})). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (h(\mathit{cry}) \simeq g(f(\mathit{cry}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, \mathit{crx}, \mathit{crl}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(g, f(\mathit{crx}), \mathit{crm}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(h, \mathit{crx}, (\mathit{crm} \cdot \mathit{crl})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{deriv-chain}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, a, l, m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, a, l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(g, f(a), m) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(\operatorname{compose}(g, f), a, (m \cdot l)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-chain}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall u, \mathit{d2s}, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, \mathit{d2s}, \mathit{d2g}, \operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2a}), \mathit{d2m}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{d2y} \in u.\; (\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2y}) \in \mathit{d2s}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, (\lambda \mathit{d2x} \in u.\; \operatorname{d2g}(\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2x}))), \mathit{d2a}, \operatorname{mul}(k)(\mathit{d2m}, \mathit{d2l})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Restated 2026-09-22 for the LOCAL derivative (the first name): f differentiable at x, g differentiable at f(x), as in the notes; that f maps a neighbourhood of x into the domain of g is PROVEN from the two hypotheses, not assumed. The composite g o f is written as any function h that agrees with t |-$>$ g(f(t)) on an open interval about x. The second name is the older form for functions TOTAL on RR; the third is the rule over a normed field on open sets.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.10}
\begin{prop}[{Vanishing of the derivative at an interior extremum}]\label{thm:interval-local-max-right-deriv-nonpos}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{interval-local-max-right-deriv-nonpos}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, f, \mathit{osx}, \mathit{osl}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}local\text{-}max\text{-}at}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b), \mathit{osx}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}right\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, \mathit{osx}, \mathit{osl}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{osl} \leq 0) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{interval-local-max-left-deriv-nonneg}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, f, \mathit{osx}, \mathit{osl}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}local\text{-}max\text{-}at}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b), \mathit{osx}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}left\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, \mathit{osx}, \mathit{osl}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (0 \leq \mathit{osl}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{interval-local-max-deriv-zero}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, f, \theta \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b), l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}local\text{-}max\text{-}at}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b), \theta) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, \theta, l) \Rightarrow (l = 0)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{interior-max-deriv-zero}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, b, \theta, l. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (\theta \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < \theta) \wedge \\ \quad (\theta < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b).\; (f(x) \leq f(\theta)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, \theta, l) \Rightarrow (l = 0)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Proven 2026-09-22 as the notes state it, sentence by sentence (the first three names): at a LOCAL maximum of a function ON [a, b], a right derivative is $<$= 0, a left derivative is $>$= 0, and at an interior point a derivative is 0. The one-sided derivatives are has-right-deriv-at and has-left-deriv-at (the notes' (5) and (6), in Caratheodory form on a half-window; the limit form of (5)/(6) is not stated: the library has no limit of a function given only on a set). The notes' Definition 2.9 as printed has the two inequalities exchanged; is-local-max-at uses f(x) $<$= f(t), the sense the notes' proof uses. The last name is the older form: f TOTAL on RR and a GLOBAL maximum on [a, b].
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.11}
\begin{thm}[{Generalized Mean Value Theorem}]\label{thm:generalized-mvt-on-interval}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{generalized-mvt-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f, g \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(g, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists m. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(g, x, m) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b), l, m. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, \theta, l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(g, \theta, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad ((l \cdot (g(b) - g(a))) = (m \cdot (f(b) - f(a)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{generalized-mvt}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, a, b. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (g \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, g, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists m.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(g, x, m) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (a < \theta) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\theta < b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l, m. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, \theta, l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(g, \theta, m) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad ((l \cdot (g(b) - g(a))) = (m \cdot (f(b) - f(a)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.12}

%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{rolle-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall h \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(h, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(h, x, l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad (h(a) = h(b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(h, \theta, 0) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{rolle}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall h, a, b. \\ \quad (h \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, h, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(h, x, l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad (h(a) = h(b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((a < \theta) \wedge ((\theta < b) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(h, \theta, 0))) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Restated 2026-09-21 for functions ON [a, b] (the first name). The derivative is the local relation has-deriv-at(f, x, l), so f'(theta) appears as a value l. The second name is the older form for functions TOTAL on RR with two-sided continuity at the endpoints; it remains as the lemma behind the first.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.13}
\begin{thm}[{Mean Value Theorem}]\label{thm:mvt-on-interval}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b), l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, \theta, l) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (l = ((f(b) - f(a)) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((b - a)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, b. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (a < \theta) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\theta < b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, \theta, l) \wedge ((l \cdot (b - a)) = (f(b) - f(a)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Restated 2026-09-21 for functions ON [a, b] (the first name). The derivative is the local relation has-deriv-at(f, x, l), so f'(theta) appears as a value l. The second name is the older form for functions TOTAL on RR with two-sided continuity at the endpoints; it remains as the lemma behind the first. The quotient of the notes is stored as (f(b) - f(a)) * recip(b - a): the reader desugars `/' when it parses.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.14}
\begin{cor}[{Increment bounds from derivative bounds}]\label{thm:mvt-upper-bound-on-interval}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt-upper-bound-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, m \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \wedge (l \leq m)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad ((f(b) - f(a)) \leq (m \cdot (b - a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt-lower-bound-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, m \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \wedge (m \leq l)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad ((m \cdot (b - a)) \leq (f(b) - f(a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt-abs-bound-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, m \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(f, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \wedge (\lvert l \rvert \leq m)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lvert (f(b) - f(a)) \rvert \leq (m \cdot (b - a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt-upper-bound}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, b, m. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (m \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \wedge (l \leq m)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad ((f(b) - f(a)) \leq (m \cdot (b - a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt-lower-bound}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, b, m. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (m \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \wedge (m \leq l)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad ((m \cdot (b - a)) \leq (f(b) - f(a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{mvt-abs-bound}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), a, b, m \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, x, l) \wedge (\lvert l \rvert \leq m)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\lvert (f(b) - f(a)) \rvert \leq (m \cdot (b - a))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Restated 2026-09-21 for functions ON [a, b] (the first three names), with the local derivative has-deriv-at. The last three names are the older forms for functions TOTAL on RR with two-sided continuity at the endpoints.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.15}
\begin{cor}[{Zero derivative implies constant}]\label{thm:deriv-zero-constant-on-interval}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{deriv-zero-constant-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall h \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(h, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pat} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(h, \mathit{pat}, 0) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pau}, \mathit{pav} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (h(\mathit{pau}) = h(\mathit{pav})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{deriv-zero-implies-constant}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, b. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, x, 0) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall u, v. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((u \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \wedge (v \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (f(u) = f(v)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{deriv-zero-const-up}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, b. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((a < x) \wedge (x < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, x, 0) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall u, v. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((u \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \wedge ((v \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \wedge (u < v))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (f(u) = f(v)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.16}
\begin{prop}[{Uniqueness of the interpolating Taylor polynomial at 0}]\label{thm:taylor-interpolant-at-zero}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, f. \\ \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}(f, \mathit{tck})(0) \in \mathbb{R}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cf}(\mathit{tck}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}(f, \mathit{tck})(0) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{tck}))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{cf}(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(x, k))), (n + 1))), \mathit{tck})(0) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}(f, \mathit{tck})(0) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tcg} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{tcg}(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(x, k))), (n + 1))), \mathit{tck})(0) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}(f, \mathit{tck})(0) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{tcg}(\mathit{tck}) = \operatorname{cf}(\mathit{tck})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

The tree has the Taylor polynomial as a functoid, taylor-poly, with the unfold r8e-tp-unfold and the two agreement facts taylor-poly-at-center and taylor-center-partial-sum (the polynomial's VALUE at the centre is f of the centre); it has no statement that its derivatives at the centre match f's, and no uniqueness statement, nor any notion of the DEGREE of a polynomial function.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.18}
\begin{thm}[{Taylor's formula with a general auxiliary function G}]\label{thm:taylor-formula-on-interval}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-formula-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{itd}, \mathit{itm} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}taylor\text{-}family}(\mathit{itd}, (\mathit{itm} + 1), a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{itg} \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(\mathit{itg}, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{itx} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \exists \mathit{itl}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(\mathit{itg}, \mathit{itx}, \mathit{itl}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{itxi} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b), \mathit{itmu}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(\mathit{itg}, \mathit{itxi}, \mathit{itmu}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad ((\mathit{itmu} \cdot \operatorname{taylor\text{-}rem}(\mathit{itd}, (\mathit{itm} + 1), a, b)) \cdot \operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{itm})) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; ((\operatorname{itd}((\mathit{itm} + 1))(\mathit{itxi}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((b - \mathit{itxi}), \mathit{itm})) \cdot (\operatorname{itg}(b) - \operatorname{itg}(a))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{itmu} \cdot \operatorname{taylor\text{-}rem}(\mathit{itd}, (\mathit{itm} + 1), a, b)) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (((\operatorname{itd}((\mathit{itm} + 1))(\mathit{itxi}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{itm}))) \cdot \operatorname{power}((b - \mathit{itxi}), \mathit{itm})) \cdot (\operatorname{itg}(b) - \operatorname{itg}(a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-lagrange}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, x, n. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{taylor\text{-}differentiable}(f, a, x, n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (a < \theta) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\theta < x) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{factorial}((n + 1)) \cdot (f(x) - \operatorname{taylor\text{-}poly}(f, a, n, x))) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}(f, (n + 1))(\theta) \cdot \operatorname{power}((x - a), (n + 1))) \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Proven 2026-09-22 for functions ON [a, b] with a general G, as in the notes (the first name); its conclusion gives (20) twice, multiplied through by (n-1)! and literally with the division. n is written succ(m). The derivatives f, f', ..., f\textasciicircum{}(n) enter as a finite family d(0), ..., d(n) (is-taylor-family): each d(k), k $<$ n, continuous on [a, b] with derivative d(k+1) on (a, b); no derivative is taken at an endpoint, where the notes speak of f\textasciicircum{}(n-1) `defined on [a, b]' (a one-sided derivative at a and b). The second name is the older Lagrange form for functions TOTAL on RR.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.19}
\begin{cor}[{Taylor's formula with Lagrange remainder}]\label{thm:taylor-lagrange-on-interval}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-lagrange-on-interval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{itd}, \mathit{itm} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}taylor\text{-}family}(\mathit{itd}, (\mathit{itm} + 1), a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{itxi} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{taylor\text{-}rem}(\mathit{itd}, (\mathit{itm} + 1), a, b) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; ((\operatorname{itd}((\mathit{itm} + 1))(\mathit{itxi}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}((\mathit{itm} + 1)))) \cdot \operatorname{power}((b - a), (\mathit{itm} + 1))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-lagrange}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, a, x, n. \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge \\ \quad (a < x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{taylor\text{-}differentiable}(f, a, x, n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \theta \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (a < \theta) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\theta < x) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{factorial}((n + 1)) \cdot (f(x) - \operatorname{taylor\text{-}poly}(f, a, n, x))) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}(f, (n + 1))(\theta) \cdot \operatorname{power}((x - a), (n + 1))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

The second name is the older form for functions TOTAL on RR, with the remainder cross-multiplied by the factorial.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.20}
\begin{cor}[{Supremum bound for the Taylor remainder}]\label{thm:taylor-remainder-sup-bound}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{tcf}, \mathit{tcm} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}taylor\text{-}family}(\mathit{tcf}, (\mathit{tcm} + 1), a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{rr\text{-}bounded\text{-}above}(\operatorname{image}((\lambda \mathit{tcv} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \lvert \operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tcm} + 1))(\mathit{tcv}) \rvert), \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{ooint}(a, b))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \lvert \operatorname{taylor\text{-}rem}(\mathit{tcf}, (\mathit{tcm} + 1), a, b) \rvert \\ \quad \quad \leq\; ((\operatorname{power}((b - a), (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}((\mathit{tcm} + 1)))) \cdot \operatorname{sup}(\operatorname{image}((\lambda \mathit{tcv} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b).\; \lvert \operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tcm} + 1))(\mathit{tcv}) \rvert), \operatorname{ooint}(a, b)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-24 (batch 25): PROVEN with ONE explicit hypothesis the notes leave implicit: the set of |f\textasciicircum{}(n)(xi)|, xi in (a, b), is bounded above (it does not follow from 2.18's hypotheses). EARLIER NOTE: No statement bounding the Taylor remainder by (b - a)\textasciicircum{}n / n! times the SUPREMUM of abs(f\textasciicircum{}(n)) over the open interval. The library has only the pointwise-witness form taylor-lagrange, and the normed-space analogues vector-taylor-remainder-bound and nvs-taylor-remainder-bound, which bound by the norm of the derivative AT THE WITNESS theta, not by a supremum; no sup over an open interval of a derivative family is formed anywhere.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.21}
\begin{cor}[{Continuous remainder factor S\_n}]\label{thm:taylor-remainder-factor}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-remainder-factor}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{tcf}, \mathit{tcm} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{tcf}(\mathit{tck}) \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} < (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(\operatorname{tcf}(\mathit{tck}), \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} < (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tcx} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(\operatorname{tcf}(\mathit{tck}), \mathit{tcx}, \operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tck} + 1))(\mathit{tcx})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(\operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tcm} + 1)), \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{tcs} \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(\mathit{tcs}, \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{tcs}(a) = \operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tcm} + 1))(a)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tct} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{taylor\text{-}rem}(\mathit{tcf}, (\mathit{tcm} + 1), a, \mathit{tct}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; ((\operatorname{tcs}(\mathit{tct}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{tct} - a), (\mathit{tcm} + 1))) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}((\mathit{tcm} + 1)))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tct} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \lvert \operatorname{tcs}(\mathit{tct}) \rvert \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{sup}(\operatorname{image}((\lambda \mathit{tcv} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \lvert \operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tcm} + 1))(\mathit{tcv}) \rvert), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{ccint}(a, b))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-lagrange-subinterval}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{tcf}, \mathit{tcm} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} \leq (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{tcf}(\mathit{tck}) \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} < (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}on}(\operatorname{tcf}(\mathit{tck}), \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{tck} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tck} < (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tcx} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{has\text{-}deriv\text{-}at}(\operatorname{tcf}(\mathit{tck}), \mathit{tcx}, \operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tck} + 1))(\mathit{tcx})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{tct} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (a < \mathit{tct}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{tct} \leq b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{tcxi} \in \operatorname{ooint}(a, \mathit{tct}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{taylor\text{-}rem}(\mathit{tcf}, (\mathit{tcm} + 1), a, \mathit{tct}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; ((\operatorname{tcf}((\mathit{tcm} + 1))(\mathit{tcxi}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}((\mathit{tcm} + 1)))) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{tct} - a), (\mathit{tcm} + 1))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

THE NOTES' "R\_n(a) = f\textasciicircum{}(n)(a)" IS A MISPRINT for S\_n(a) = f\textasciicircum{}(n)(a). EARLIER NOTE: Nothing constructs a continuous function S\_n on [a, b] with R\_n(t) = S\_n(t)(t - a)\textasciicircum{}n / n!, nothing states S\_n(a) = f\textasciicircum{}(n)(a) or the bound abs(S\_n(t)) $<$= sup over [a, b] of abs(f\textasciicircum{}(n)). The nearest machinery is the Caratheodory-style witness used for is-diff-at itself (the phi of the definition, and diff-at-witness-family), which produces a continuous factor for the FIRST-order increment only.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.22}
\begin{prop}[{Taylor's formula is exact for a polynomial}]\label{thm:taylor-exact-polynomial}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{tcm} \in \mathbb{N}, \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}), a, h \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{cf}(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(x, k))), (\mathit{tcm} + 1)))((a + h)) \\ \quad =\; \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda \mathit{tci} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad ((\operatorname{nth\text{-}deriv}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}((\lambda k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{cf}(k) \cdot \operatorname{power}(x, k))), (\mathit{tcm} + 1))), \mathit{tci})(a) \cdot \operatorname{power}(h, \mathit{tci})) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{tci})))), \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{tcm} + 1)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-24 (batch 25): PROVEN for h of EITHER sign, by induction on the degree (the notes' route through the Lagrange form covers only a $<$ b, i.e. h $>$ 0). EARLIER NOTE: No statement that a polynomial function of degree n equals its own order-n Taylor expansion about an arbitrary centre. There is no predicate for being a polynomial function nor any notion of degree; polynomial functions appear only as the explicit term vnb-lambda(x, rr, series-partial-sum(vnb-lambda(k, nn, cf(k) * x\textasciicircum{}k), succ(n))), for which deriv-polynomial and poly-antiderivative are proven. The carrier carr(poly(a)) is the ALGEBRAIC polynomial ring (finitely supported sequences), which is not connected to that function term by any theorem.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.24}
\begin{prop}[{Mean Value Theorem for a directional derivative}]\label{thm:dir-deriv-mvt}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{dir-deriv-mvt}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, f, a, \eta. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}vector\text{-}space}(m) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{vec}(m) \to \mathbb{R})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\eta \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{seg\text{-}curve}(m, f, a, \eta), x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((0 < x) \wedge (x < 1))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(\operatorname{seg\text{-}curve}(m, f, a, \eta), x, l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{th} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{th}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{th} < 1) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{dv}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, \operatorname{vadd}(m)(a, \operatorname{act}(m)(\mathit{th}, \eta)), \eta, \mathit{dv}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{dv} = (f(\operatorname{vadd}(m)(a, \eta)) - f(a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{dir-deriv-increment}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}vector\text{-}space}(m) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f \in (\operatorname{vec}(m) \to \mathbb{R}), \beta, \mathit{zeta} \in \operatorname{vec}(m). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{vec}(m). \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, x, \mathit{zeta}, k) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{th} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{th}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{th} < 1) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (f(\operatorname{vadd}(m)(\beta, \mathit{zeta})) - f(\beta)) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{dir\text{-}deriv}(m, f, \operatorname{vadd}(m)(\beta, \operatorname{act}(m)(\mathit{th}, \mathit{zeta})), \mathit{zeta}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} There is no open set U in the library statements. dir-deriv-mvt requires f in fun(vec(m), rr), i.e. f TOTAL on the normed vector space, and replaces the hypothesis that the partial derivative is defined on U by hypotheses on the SEGMENT CURVE seg-curve(m, f, a, eta): two-sided continuity at every point of ccint(0, 1), including the endpoints 0 and 1, and differentiability at every interior point. dir-deriv-increment is the closer match in shape -- it concludes f(b + zeta) - f(b) = dir-deriv(m, f, b + th * zeta, zeta) for some th in (0, 1) -- but it asks that the directional derivative in direction zeta exist at EVERY point of vec(m), where the notes ask only that it be defined on U with the segment [a, a + eta] inside U. The ambient space is an arbitrary normed vector space, not the specific E = R\textasciicircum{}n of the notes.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.25}
\begin{lem}[{Homogeneity of the directional derivative}]\label{thm:dir-deriv-homogeneous}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, f, a, \eta, \mathit{lam}, \mathit{dl}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}vector\text{-}space}(m) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{vec}(m) \to \mathbb{R})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\eta \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{lam} \in \mathbb{R}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \eta, \mathit{dl}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \operatorname{act}(m)(\mathit{lam}, \eta), (\mathit{lam} \cdot \mathit{dl})) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (38 steps; 10 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-dir-diff-at, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact nvs-act-in-vec, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact seg-curve-in-fun, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact rr-mul-closed, 3 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact seg-curve-apply, 6 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(subst 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact seg-curve-apply, 6 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(subst 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact nvs-act-scale-assoc, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(subst 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(crs)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(subst 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(qrfl)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac is-dir-diff-at, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact dir-diff-scale, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{nvs-act-in-vec}, \texttt{seg-curve-in-fun}, \texttt{rr-mul-closed}, \texttt{seg-curve-apply}, \texttt{nvs-act-scale-assoc}, \texttt{dir-diff-scale}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{crs}, \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%

%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} f is required to be in fun(vec(m), rr), i.e. TOTAL on the normed vector space, where the notes ask that f and d\_eta f be defined on a neighbourhood of a. In the other direction the library is MORE general: it needs only is-dir-diff-at(m, f, a, eta, dl) at the single point a, not that d\_eta f be defined on a whole neighbourhood. The ambient space is an arbitrary normed vector space, not E = R\textasciicircum{}n. Neither statement guards lambda against 0, although the notes' proof divides by lambda.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.26}
\begin{lem}[{Additivity of the directional derivative under continuity}]\label{thm:dir-deriv-additive}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, f, a, \eta, \xi, \mathit{dl}, \mathit{dm}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}vector\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{vec}(m) \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad (\eta \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad (\xi \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \eta, \mathit{dl}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \xi, \mathit{dm}) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{vec}(m). \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, x, \eta, k) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{vec}(m). \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, x, \xi, k) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{nvs\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m), \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \\ \quad \quad (\lambda x \in \operatorname{vec}(m).\; \operatorname{dir\text{-}deriv}(m, f, x, \eta)), a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{nvs\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m), \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \\ \quad \quad (\lambda x \in \operatorname{vec}(m).\; \operatorname{dir\text{-}deriv}(m, f, x, \xi)), a) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \operatorname{vadd}(m)(\eta, \xi), (\mathit{dl} + \mathit{dm})) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (51 steps; 10 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact rr-zero-in, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact rr-one-in, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac <, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(arith)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact dir-diff-value-in-rr, 6 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact dir-diff-value-in-rr, 6 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact nvs-vadd-in-vec, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact seg-curve-in-fun, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus-id 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact rr-add-closed, 3 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact dir-quotient-in-fun, 8 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact dir-quotient-at-zero, 8 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact dir-quotient-continuous, 8 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact dir-quotient-identity, 8 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(inst+ 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac is-dir-diff-at, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact diff-at-local, 6 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{rr-zero-in}, \texttt{rr-one-in}, \texttt{dir-diff-value-in-rr}, \texttt{nvs-vadd-in-vec}, \texttt{seg-curve-in-fun}, \texttt{rr-add-closed}, \texttt{dir-quotient-in-fun}, \texttt{dir-quotient-at-zero}, \texttt{dir-quotient-continuous}, \texttt{dir-quotient-identity}, \texttt{diff-at-local}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{crs}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} f is required to be in fun(vec(m), rr), i.e. TOTAL on the normed vector space, and the existence hypothesis is global: forall x in vec(m). forsome k. is-dir-diff-at(m, f, x, eta, k), and likewise for xi, where the notes ask only that d\_eta f and d\_xi f exist in a NEIGHBOURHOOD of a. The continuity hypothesis is stated at the single point a -- is-continuous-at of the maps x |-$>$ dir-deriv(m, f, x, eta) and x |-$>$ dir-deriv(m, f, x, xi) at a -- where the notes ask for continuity throughout the neighbourhood. The ambient space is an arbitrary normed vector space, not E = R\textasciicircum{}n. The conclusion, that d\_(eta + xi) f(a) is DEFINED and equals the sum, is carried by the relational is-dir-diff-at and so is faithful.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.27}
\begin{prop}[{Linearity of the directional derivative on the span}]\label{thm:dir-deriv-linear}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall m, f, a, \eta, \xi, r, s, \mathit{dl}, \mathit{dm}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}vector\text{-}space}(m) \wedge \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{vec}(m) \to \mathbb{R})) \wedge \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad (\eta \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad (\xi \in \operatorname{vec}(m)) \wedge \\ \quad (r \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (s \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \eta, \mathit{dl}) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \xi, \mathit{dm}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{vec}(m). \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, x, \operatorname{act}(m)(r, \eta), k) \wedge \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{vec}(m). \exists k. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, x, \operatorname{act}(m)(s, \xi), k) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{nvs\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m), \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \\ \quad \quad (\lambda x \in \operatorname{vec}(m).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{dir\text{-}deriv}(m, f, x, \operatorname{act}(m)(r, \eta))), \\ \quad \quad a) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{nvs\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(m), \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \\ \quad \quad (\lambda x \in \operatorname{vec}(m).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{dir\text{-}deriv}(m, f, x, \operatorname{act}(m)(s, \xi))), \\ \quad \quad a) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dir\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(m, f, a, \operatorname{vadd}(m)(\operatorname{act}(m)(r, \eta), \operatorname{act}(m)(s, \xi)), \\ \quad \quad \quad ((r \cdot \mathit{dl}) + (s \cdot \mathit{dm}))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The notes quantify over ALL x in U and ALL phi in the vector space V generated by eta and xi, and assert that phi |-$>$ d\_phi f(x) is a linear MAP. dir-deriv-linear states only the single instance at the single point a: from is-dir-diff-at at a in directions eta and xi it concludes is-dir-diff-at(m, f, a, r*eta + s*xi, r*dl + s*dm), and it does so under extra hypotheses the notes do not carry at that level -- that the directional derivatives in directions r*eta and s*xi exist at EVERY point of vec(m) and that the two derivative maps are continuous at a. f is required total on vec(m). No span or generated-subspace vocabulary is used, and no statement says the assignment is linear as a map.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.28}
\begin{prop}[{Continuous partials give a directional derivative in every direction}]\label{thm:calculus-2.28}
%
\textit{U contained in E, f: U --$>$ R, and d\_(e\_i) f(x) for i = 1, ..., n defined and continuous as functions of x in U: then for all eta in E and x in U, d\_eta f(x) is defined, is linear in eta and continuous in x.}

Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}

%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}

\end{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The space E = R\textasciicircum{}n with the sup norm max(abs(eta\_1), ..., abs(eta\_n)) does not exist in the library, and neither do the unit basis vectors e\_i nor the partial derivatives d\_(e\_i) f. The nearest facts are the two-direction lemmas dir-deriv-additive and dir-deriv-homogeneous over an abstract normed vector space, which are what an induction on k would use; the induction over a basis, the conclusion that d\_eta f is linear in eta, and the conclusion that it is continuous in x are all absent.

\textit{f such that the partial derivatives d\_(e\_i) f(x) are defined and continuous in x in a neighborhood of a: then for any eps $>$ 0 there is delta such that for norm(eta) $<$= delta, abs(f(a + eta) - f(a) - sum over i of eta\_i d\_(e\_i) f(a)) $<$= norm(eta) eps.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}

\begin{proof}

The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Nothing states total differentiability of a function on R\textasciicircum{}n from the continuity of its partial derivatives; there is no R\textasciicircum{}n with the sup norm, no basis vectors e\_i, no Df(a) = (d\_(e\_1) f(a), ..., d\_(e\_n) f(a)), and no estimate of the form abs(f(a + eta) - f(a) - sum eta\_i d\_(e\_i) f(a)) $<$= norm(eta) eps. The whole first-order differentiability theory in the tree is scalar: is-diff-at over RR and is-diff-on over a normed field. CLAUDE.md records Props 2.28 and 2.29 as the next terrain, after the metric subspace structure.

\begin{prop}[{Unions and finite intersections of open sets}]\label{thm:union-of-opens-open}

\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.9}
\begin{prop}[{Closed sets are exactly those stable under limits of sequences}]\label{thm:closed-limit-in}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{closed-limit-in}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall a. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to a), l. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, f, l) \Rightarrow (l \in a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{closed-set-limit-in}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, a, f, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, f, l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f(n) \in a) \Rightarrow (l \in a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{closed-set-limit-in-tail}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{av}, \mathit{fv}, \mathit{lv}, \mathit{nb}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, \mathit{av}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, \mathit{fv}, \mathit{lv}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{nb} \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad ((\mathit{nb} \leq n) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{fv}(n) \in \mathit{av})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{lv} \in \mathit{av}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.10}
\begin{prop}[{A set is closed if and only if it contains its accumulation points}]\label{thm:calculus-3.10}
%
\textit{A necessary and sufficient condition that A subset X be closed is that it contain all its accumulation points, x being an accumulation point of A when every ball B(x,r) contains an element of A distinct from x.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}

The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}

\end{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The library has no notion of accumulation point (cluster-point is for SEQUENCES, not for sets), and no statement of this equivalence. The nearest facts are about the closure: closure-membership (x in closure(s,a) iff x in pts(s) and every open u containing x meets a), closure-is-closed, closure-contains and closure-in-closed.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.12}
\begin{prop}[{Four equivalent characterizations of a compact metric space}]\label{thm:compact-iff-fip}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-iff-fip}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow \forall c.\; (\operatorname{has\text{-}fip}(s, c) \Rightarrow \exists p.\; (p \in \operatorname{intersection\text{-}of}(c)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-iff-cluster-point}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{pts}(s)).\; \exists x.\; \operatorname{cluster\text{-}point}(s, f, x)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-iff-seq-compact}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow \operatorname{seq\text{-}compact}(s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-iff-tb-complete}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow (\operatorname{totally\text{-}bounded}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(s))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

The finite intersection property is relativised to the library predicate has-fip(s,c), which adds two hypotheses the notes do not make: the family c must be INHABITED (forsome a0, a0 in c), and only INHABITED finite subfamilies f are required to have a common point, so the notes' case F = empty (which forces X non-empty) is not covered. The library also proves the sequentially-compact form compact-iff-seq-compact (every sequence has a CONVERGENT SUBSEQUENCE), which the notes do not state; their clause (3) is compact-iff-cluster-point.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.14}
\begin{prop}[{Continuity at a point is sequential continuity}]\label{thm:continuous-at-iff-sequential}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{continuous-at-iff-sequential}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, f, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(t) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \operatorname{pts}(t))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{pts}(s)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(s, t, f, a) \Leftrightarrow \forall \mathit{sq} \in \operatorname{pts}(s)^{\mathbb{N}}.\; (\operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, \mathit{sq}, a) \Rightarrow \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(t, \operatorname{compose}(f, \mathit{sq}), f(a)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{continuous-at-implies-sequential}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, f, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(t) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \operatorname{pts}(t))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{pts}(s)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(s, t, f, a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{sq} \in \operatorname{pts}(s)^{\mathbb{N}}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, \mathit{sq}, a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(t, \operatorname{compose}(f, \mathit{sq}), f(a)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.15}
\begin{prop}[{Continuity equals closedness (openness) of preimages}]\label{thm:continuous-implies-closed-preimage}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{continuous-implies-closed-preimage}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, t, f) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall a. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(t, a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, \operatorname{preimage}(s, f, a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{closed-preimage-implies-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(t) \wedge \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \operatorname{pts}(t))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall a. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(t, a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}closed}(s, \operatorname{preimage}(s, f, a)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, t, f) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{continuous-implies-open-preimage}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, t, f) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall v. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(t, v) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(s, \operatorname{preimage}(s, f, v)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{open-preimage-implies-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(t) \wedge \\ \quad (f \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \operatorname{pts}(t))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall v. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(t, v) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}open}(s, \operatorname{preimage}(s, f, v)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, t, f) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.16}
\begin{lem}[{Subsequence principle}]\label{thm:subsequence-principle}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, f, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{pts}(s))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (l \in \operatorname{pts}(s)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \varphi. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{strictly\text{-}mono\text{-}nn}(\varphi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists \psi. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{strictly\text{-}mono\text{-}nn}(\psi) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, \operatorname{subseq}(\operatorname{subseq}(f, \varphi), \psi), l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, f, l) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.19}
\begin{prop}[{The continuous image of a compact set is compact}]\label{thm:continuous-image-of-compact}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{continuous-image-of-compact}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, \mathit{fqf}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, t, \mathit{fqf}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{aqa}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{aqa} \subseteq \operatorname{pts}(s)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(s, \mathit{aqa})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(t, \operatorname{image}(\mathit{fqf}, \mathit{aqa}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-image}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, t, \mathit{fqf}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, t, \mathit{fqf}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(\operatorname{subspace\text{-}ms}(t, \operatorname{image}(\mathit{fqf}, \operatorname{pts}(s)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.21}
\begin{prop}[{A continuous function on a compact space is uniformly continuous}]\label{thm:continuous-uniformly-continuous-on-ccint}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{eps}. \\ \quad (a \leq b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \delta \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \delta) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall p, q \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lvert (p - q) \rvert \leq \delta) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lvert (f(p) - f(q)) \rvert \leq \mathit{eps}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The general metric-space statement is absent. What exists is the single special case X = a closed bounded interval of RR, Y = RR, and it deviates in three ways: f is required to be in fun(rr, rr), i.e. TOTAL on RR, with continuity assumed at every x in ccint(a, b) and hence TWO-SIDED at the endpoints a and b; the conclusion is spelled out epsilon-delta inline (for a given eps there is d\_ $>$ 0 with abs(f(p\_) - f(q\_)) $<$= eps for p\_, q\_ in ccint(a, b) at distance $<$= d\_) and does NOT use the library's own is-uniformly-continuous predicate; and the epsilon is a PARAMETER of the theorem rather than universally quantified inside it. The guard is a $<$= b, so the degenerate interval a = b is allowed.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.22}
\begin{prop}[{Continuity plus uniform continuity off a compact set gives uniform continuity}]\label{thm:calculus-3.22}
%
\textit{Suppose X, Y are metric spaces and f : X --$>$ Y is continuous.  If K subset X is compact and f is uniformly continuous on X \textbackslash{} K, then f is uniformly continuous.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.26}
\begin{prop}[{Unique uniformly continuous extension from a dense subspace}]\label{thm:calculus-3.26}
%
\textit{Suppose X, Y are metric spaces, A subset X is a dense subspace and Y is complete.  Then every uniformly continuous function f : A --$>$ Y has a unique extension to a uniformly continuous function fbar : X --$>$ Y.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} No extension theorem for uniformly continuous maps, and no EXISTENCE or UNIQUENESS statement for an extension along a dense subspace. The library does have the metric completion (completion-is-metric-space, completion-is-complete, embed-isometry, embed-in-fun) and a density notion for sequences (is-dense-seq), but no theorem connects them to an extension; the only extends-on facts in the whole library are the Hahn-Banach ones (hahn-banach, hahn-banach-extend-one, hb-extend-construct).
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.27}
\begin{prop}[{min(d,1) is a metric, with the same convergent sequences}]\label{thm:trunc-metric-is-metric-space}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{trunc-metric-is-metric-space}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(\operatorname{trunc\text{-}metric}(s)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{trunc-metric-dist}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, u, v \in \operatorname{pts}(s). \\ \quad (\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{trunc\text{-}metric}(s))(u, v) \simeq \operatorname{min}(1, \operatorname{dist}(s)(u, v))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{trunc-metric-id-uniformly-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}uniformly\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{trunc\text{-}metric}(s), (\lambda \alpha \in \operatorname{pts}(s).\; \alpha)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{trunc-metric-id-uniformly-continuous-back}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}uniformly\text{-}continuous}(\operatorname{trunc\text{-}metric}(s), s, (\lambda \alpha \in \operatorname{pts}(s).\; \alpha)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bdd-metric-converges-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{pts}(s)), \ell \in \operatorname{pts}(s). \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{bdd\text{-}metric}(s), f, \ell) \Leftrightarrow \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(s, f, \ell)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The two halves are proven for DIFFERENT truncations. trunc-metric(s) is literally the notes' min(1, d) (trunc-metric-dist) and is proven to be a metric space, but for it the library offers only the uniform continuity of the identity in both directions, never the convergence equivalence. The convergence equivalence that IS proven, bdd-metric-converges-iff, is for bdd-metric(s) = d/(1 + d), which is not the notes' d'. So no single library object carries both conclusions of Proposition 3.27.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.28}
\begin{prop}[{Tychonov Theorem for Metric Spaces}]\label{thm:compact-countable-product}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-countable-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{ms}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ms\text{-}sequence}(\mathit{ms}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(\operatorname{ms}(n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(\operatorname{product\text{-}metric}(\mathit{ms})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{seq-compact-countable-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{ms}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ms\text{-}sequence}(\mathit{ms}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{seq\text{-}compact}(\operatorname{ms}(n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{seq\text{-}compact}(\operatorname{product\text{-}metric}(\mathit{ms})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{compact-countable-product}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (22 steps; 8 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(inst+ 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-ms-sequence, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(inst+ 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac compact-iff-seq-compact-rev, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact product-metric-default-summable, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact product-is-metric-space, 3 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact seq-compact-countable-product, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac compact-iff-seq-compact, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}

%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The product metric is FIXED by the library rather than chosen in the proof: product-metric(ms) is product-metric-w with the weight n |--$>$ 1/2\textasciicircum{}(n+1) and, in each factor, the truncation bdd-metric = d/(1+d), NOT the notes' min(d, 1) with weights 2\textasciicircum{}-k. The countable family is presented as is-ms-sequence(ms), a function on nn, rather than as a countable family \{X\_k\}. Compactness of every factor is the hypothesis forall n in nn, is-compact(ms(n)).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.33}
\begin{prop}[{On a compact space pointwise and uniform convergence agree on an equicontinuous set}]\label{thm:ptwise-cauchy-compact-equicont-unif}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{ptwise-cauchy-compact-equicont-unif}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}equicontinuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ptwise\text{-}cauchy}(s, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}unif\text{-}cauchy}(s, \mathit{fam}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{unif-cauchy-cont-implies-uniform-limit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R})). \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{fam}(k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}unif\text{-}cauchy}(s, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists g \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, g) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}uniformly}(s, \mathit{fam}, g) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{uniform-limit-continuous}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R})), g \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{fam}(k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}uniformly}(s, \mathit{fam}, g) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, g) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
