\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The equivalence itself is not stated. The library proves only the CAUCHY form -- an equicontinuous family on a compact space that is pointwise Cauchy is uniformly Cauchy -- plus, separately, that a uniformly Cauchy family of continuous functions has a continuous uniform limit. Two further restrictions: the target is fixed to rr-ms, the family being typed fam in fun(nn, fun(pts(s), rr)), where the notes allow an arbitrary metric space Y; and the object is a SEQUENCE indexed by nn, where the notes speak of an arbitrary SET E of functions and its topology. The easy converse (uniform implies pointwise) is not stated either.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.34}
\begin{prop}[{Ascoli-Arzela}]\label{thm:ascoli-arzela-sequential}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{ascoli-arzela-sequential}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \exists x.\; (x \in \operatorname{pts}(s)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{fam}(k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}equicontinuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{pointwise\text{-}bounded}(s, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{del}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{strictly\text{-}mono\text{-}nn}(\mathit{del}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists g \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, g) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}uniformly}(s, \operatorname{subseq}(\mathit{fam}, \mathit{del}), g) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{ascoli-sequential-from-diagonal}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \exists x.\; (x \in \operatorname{pts}(s)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{fam}(k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}equicontinuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{pointwise\text{-}bounded}(s, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dseq}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dense\text{-}seq}(s, \mathit{dseq}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{del}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{strictly\text{-}mono\text{-}nn}(\mathit{del}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}on}(s, \operatorname{subseq}(\mathit{fam}, \mathit{del}), \mathit{dseq}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{del}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{strictly\text{-}mono\text{-}nn}(\mathit{del}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists g \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, g) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}uniformly}(s, \operatorname{subseq}(\mathit{fam}, \mathit{del}), g) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{ascoli-pointwise-diagonal}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam}. \\ \quad \operatorname{pointwise\text{-}bounded}(s, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{dseq}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dense\text{-}seq}(s, \mathit{dseq}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{del}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{strictly\text{-}mono\text{-}nn}(\mathit{del}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}on}(s, \operatorname{subseq}(\mathit{fam}, \mathit{del}), \mathit{dseq}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{ascoli-arzela-sequential}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (10 steps; 3 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact ascoli-pointwise-diagonal, 3 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact ascoli-sequential-from-diagonal, 3 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}

%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} A SEQUENTIAL form, not the notes' relative compactness in the topology of uniform convergence: the library states that an equicontinuous, pointwise-bounded sequence of continuous functions on a compact X has a subsequence converging UNIFORMLY to a continuous limit. Four differences. (a) Y is fixed to rr-ms; the notes allow any compact metric Y. (b) pointwise-bounded(s, fam) is an added hypothesis, free in the notes because Y is compact. (c) X must be INHABITED -- forsome x, x in pts(s) -- an added guard against the empty metric space. (d) Only SUFFICIENCY is proven; the notes' necessity half, that a relatively compact set is equicontinuous, is absent, and with no relative-compactness notion in the library it cannot be stated.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.36}
\begin{lem}[{Equicontinuous sequence converging on a dense set converges everywhere, with continuous limit}]\label{thm:ascoli-dense-bridge}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{ascoli-dense-bridge}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{fam}(k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}equicontinuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \exists \mathit{dseq}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dense\text{-}seq}(s, \mathit{dseq}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}on}(s, \mathit{fam}, \mathit{dseq}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists g \in (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, g) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}uniformly}(s, \mathit{fam}, g) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{equicont-dense-conv-implies-unif-cauchy}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R}))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}equicontinuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \exists \mathit{dseq}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dense\text{-}seq}(s, \mathit{dseq}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}on}(s, \mathit{fam}, \mathit{dseq}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}unif\text{-}cauchy}(s, \mathit{fam}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{equicont-dense-conv-ptwise-cauchy}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s, \mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{pts}(s) \to \mathbb{R})). \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}equicontinuous}(s, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \mathit{fam}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \exists \mathit{dseq}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}dense\text{-}seq}(s, \mathit{dseq}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}on}(s, \mathit{fam}, \mathit{dseq}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ptwise\text{-}cauchy}(s, \mathit{fam}) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}

The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Y is fixed to rr-ms, so the notes' hypothesis that Y be a complete metric space is discharged by the completeness of RR rather than assumed; a general complete Y is not available. The dense set D is presented as a dense SEQUENCE is-dense-seq(s, dseq) rather than as a dense subset, and convergence on it as converges-on(s, fam, dseq). The library's conclusion is UNIFORM convergence to a continuous g, which is stronger than the notes' pointwise conclusion plus continuity of the limit. fam must be typed fam in fun(nn, fun(pts(s), rr)) and each fam(k) assumed is-continuous, where the notes assume only equicontinuity of the sequence.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.37}
\begin{prop}[{The isometry group of a compact metric space is compact}]\label{thm:calculus-3.37}
%
\textit{If X is a compact metric space and Gamma is the group of isometric isomorphisms phi : X --$>$ X with d\_Gamma(phi, psi) = sup\_\{x in X\} d\_X(phi(x), psi(x)), then Gamma with d\_Gamma is a compact metric space.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} is-isometry(s, t, f) is defined, but there is no group of isometric isomorphisms of a space, no sup metric d\_Gamma(phi, psi) = sup\_x d(phi(x), psi(x)) on such a set, and no compactness statement about either.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.38}
\begin{prop}[{In the isometry group uniform and pointwise convergence agree}]\label{thm:calculus-3.38}
%
\textit{Let Gamma be as in 3.37 and \{g\_i : i in N\} a sequence of elements of Gamma.  Then g\_i --$>$ g uniformly if and only if g\_i(x) --$>$ g(x) for all x in X.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}
%
\end{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.5}
\begin{prop}[{Regulated functions are exactly the uniform limits of step functions}]\label{thm:regulated-on-is-step-limit}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{regulated-on-is-step-limit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, f. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regulated\text{-}on}(f, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{fam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}step\text{-}fn}(\operatorname{fam}(k), a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}unif\text{-}limit\text{-}on}(\mathit{fam}, \operatorname{extend\text{-}const}(f, a, b), a, b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{regulated-on-step-approx}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{rswa}, \mathit{rswb}, \mathit{rswf}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regulated\text{-}on}(\mathit{rswf}, \mathit{rswa}, \mathit{rswb}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{rswe}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{rswe}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{rsth} \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}step\text{-}fn}(\mathit{rsth}, \mathit{rswa}, \mathit{rswb}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{rsqz} \in \operatorname{ccint}(\mathit{rswa}, \mathit{rswb}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \lvert (\operatorname{extend\text{-}const}(\mathit{rswf}, \mathit{rswa}, \mathit{rswb})(\mathit{rsqz}) - \operatorname{rsth}(\mathit{rsqz})) \rvert \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \leq\; \mathit{rswe} \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{uniform-limit-of-regulated}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{fam}, g, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}unif\text{-}limit\text{-}on}(\mathit{fam}, g, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}regulated}(\operatorname{fam}(k), a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regulated}(g, a, b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{continuous-is-regulated}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}regulated}(f, a, b) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-23 (batch 22-A): NECESSITY is proven ON [a, b] -- regulated-on-is-step-limit: a function regulated on [a, b] (is-regulated-on, structure-library/regulated-primitive.scm, for f in fun(ccint(a, b), rr)) is the uniform limit on [a, b] of a sequence of step functions (is-step-fn, total), the limit stated through extend-const(f, a, b) because is-unif-limit-on is total; by the creeping argument, no finite subcover. SUFFICIENCY remains only in the total form uniform-limit-of-regulated. EARLIER NOTE: NEITHER direction of the notes' equivalence is stated.  is-step-fn is defined in the library but NO theorem anywhere mentions it, so necessity (a regulated function is a uniform limit of step functions) is absent, and sufficiency is present only in the weakened form uniform-limit-of-regulated: a uniform limit of REGULATED functions is regulated. Separately, is-regulated(f, a, b) types f in fun(rr, rr), i.e. TOTAL on RR, with a and b as parameters, where the notes have f : [a,b] --$>$ R; it demands a $<$ b strictly; and it demands a right limit only where x\_ $<$ b and a left limit only where a $<$ x\_, where the notes (Remark 4.2) instead declare f(a-) = f(a) and f(b+) = f(b) so that all four one-sided limits exist.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.8}
\begin{prop}[{The antiderivable functions on [a,b] form a vector space}]\label{thm:antiderivable-add}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivable-add}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \varphi, \psi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\psi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (\varphi(x) + \psi(x))), a, b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivable-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c \in \mathbb{R}, \varphi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (c \cdot \varphi(x))), a, b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivable-sub}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \varphi, \psi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\psi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (\varphi(x) - \psi(x))), a, b) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{antiderivable-add}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (11 steps; 7 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-antiderivable, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-antiderivable, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac is-antiderivable, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ew 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact antiderivative-add, 7 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{antiderivative-add}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{crs}, \texttt{arith}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{antiderivable-scale}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (9 steps; 7 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-antiderivable, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac is-antiderivable, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ew 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact antiderivative-scale, 6 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}

\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (11 steps; 7 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-antiderivable, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-antiderivable, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac is-antiderivable, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ew 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact antiderivative-sub, 7 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Stated as three closure properties -- sum, scalar multiple and difference -- and not as a vector space: the library has no vector-space structure on a class of functions to name, so the conclusion of the notes has no counterpart. The functions are in fun(rr, rr), TOTAL on RR, with a and b as parameters, and is-antiderivable(phi, a, b) demands a $<$ b strictly, so the degenerate interval is excluded. The sum is written as the explicit term vnb-lambda(x, rr, phi(x) + psi(x)).
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.10}
\begin{prop}[{Two antiderivatives of the same function differ by a constant}]\label{thm:pw-antiderivative-differ-by-some-constant}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-differ-by-some-constant}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{pwf}, \mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{pbc} \in \mathbb{R}. \forall \mathit{pbs} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pwf}(\mathit{pbs}) = (\operatorname{paw}(\mathit{pbs}) + \mathit{pbc})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-differ-by-constant}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{pwf}, \mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pbs} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pwf}(\mathit{pbs}) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{paw}(\mathit{pbs}) + (\operatorname{pwf}(a) - \operatorname{paw}(a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivative-differ-by-constant}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, \varphi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(f, \varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(g, \varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{cst} \in \mathbb{R}. \forall s \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad (f(s) = (g(s) + \mathit{cst})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.11}
\begin{cor}[{The endpoint difference is the same for all antiderivatives}]\label{thm:pw-antiderivative-endpoint-difference}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-endpoint-difference}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{pwf}, \mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad ((\operatorname{pwf}(b) - \operatorname{pwf}(a)) = (\operatorname{paw}(b) - \operatorname{paw}(a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivative-endpoint-difference}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, \varphi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(f, \varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(g, \varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad ((f(b) - f(a)) = (g(b) - g(a))) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.12}
\begin{prop}[{The definite integral is a linear functional}]\label{thm:pw-antiderivative-linear}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-linear}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b, \mathit{pcc}, \mathit{pdd} \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{pwf}, \mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, \mathit{ppsi}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{paw}, \mathit{ppsi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi} \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pauh}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq ((\mathit{pcc} \cdot \operatorname{pwf}(\mathit{pay})) + (\mathit{pdd} \cdot \operatorname{paw}(\mathit{pay})))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pchi}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq ((\mathit{pcc} \cdot \operatorname{pphi}(\mathit{pay})) + (\mathit{pdd} \cdot \operatorname{ppsi}(\mathit{pay})))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi}, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pchi} \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; ((\mathit{pcc} \cdot \int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pphi}) + (\mathit{pdd} \cdot \int_{a}^{b} \mathit{ppsi})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{pwf}, \mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, \mathit{ppsi}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{paw}, \mathit{ppsi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi} \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pauh}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq (\operatorname{pwf}(\mathit{pay}) + \operatorname{paw}(\mathit{pay}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pchi}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq (\operatorname{pphi}(\mathit{pay}) + \operatorname{ppsi}(\mathit{pay}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi}, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pchi} = (\int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pphi} + \int_{a}^{b} \mathit{ppsi})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-real-mul}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, \mathit{pcc} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi} \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pauh}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq (\mathit{pcc} \cdot \operatorname{pwf}(\mathit{pay}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pchi}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq (\mathit{pcc} \cdot \operatorname{pphi}(\mathit{pay}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi}, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pchi} = (\mathit{pcc} \cdot \int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pphi})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{c-int-add}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \varphi, \psi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\psi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \int_{a}^{b} (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (\varphi(x) + \psi(x))) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\int_{a}^{b} \varphi + \int_{a}^{b} \psi) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{c-int-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall c \in \mathbb{R}, \varphi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\int_{a}^{b} (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (c \cdot \varphi(x))) = (c \cdot \int_{a}^{b} \varphi)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-linear}}}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-23: pw-antiderivative-linear (batch 18-A) states Prop 4.12 in ONE formula; since batch 20 (2026-09-23) the primitive is is-primitive with a COUNTABLE exceptional set (Dieudonne VIII.7), of which the notes' Definition 4.6 (no exceptional set) is a special case. EARLIER NOTE: Restated 2026-09-22 for functions ON [a, b] (the first name(s)), for the PIECEWISE primitive is-pw-antiderivative: continuous on [a, b], with derivative phi(t) at every t of (a, b) outside a finite set (Dieudonne 8.7 with a finite exceptional set; the notes' Definition 4.6 is the case of an empty exceptional set, which the library does not single out yet). `Linear functional' is given as two theorems, the sum and the real multiple: the space of antiderivable functions is not a structure in the library. The remaining names are the older forms for functions TOTAL on RR (is-antiderivative, c-int); they remain in the library.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.13}
\begin{prop}[{The integral of a sum is the sum of the integrals}]\label{thm:pw-antiderivative-sum}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{pw-antiderivative-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \mathit{pwf}, \mathit{paw}, \mathit{pphi}, \mathit{ppsi}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pwf}, \mathit{pphi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{paw}, \mathit{ppsi}, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi} \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pauh}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq (\operatorname{pwf}(\mathit{pay}) + \operatorname{paw}(\mathit{pay}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pay} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{pchi}(\mathit{pay}) \simeq (\operatorname{pphi}(\mathit{pay}) + \operatorname{ppsi}(\mathit{pay}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pauh}, \mathit{pchi}, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pchi} = (\int_{a}^{b} \mathit{pphi} + \int_{a}^{b} \mathit{ppsi})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{c-int-add}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \varphi, \psi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\psi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \int_{a}^{b} (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (\varphi(x) + \psi(x))) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\int_{a}^{b} \varphi + \int_{a}^{b} \psi) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivative-add}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f, g, \varphi, \psi, a, b. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(f, \varphi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(g, \psi, a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}((\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (f(x) + g(x))), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (\varphi(x) + \psi(x))), a, b) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Restated 2026-09-22 for functions ON [a, b] (the first name(s)), for the PIECEWISE primitive is-pw-antiderivative: continuous on [a, b], with derivative phi(t) at every t of (a, b) outside a finite set (Dieudonne 8.7 with a finite exceptional set; the notes' Definition 4.6 is the case of an empty exceptional set, which the library does not single out yet). The remaining names are the older forms for functions TOTAL on RR (is-antiderivative, c-int); they remain in the library.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.16}
\begin{prop}[{Differentiating a sequence whose derivatives converge uniformly}]\label{thm:primitive-uniform-limit}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{primitive-uniform-limit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{gfam}, \mathit{ffam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R})), f \in (\operatorname{ccint}(a, b) \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{puk} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\operatorname{gfam}(\mathit{puk}), \operatorname{ffam}(\mathit{puk}), a, b) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{eps}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{pun} \in \mathbb{N}. \forall \mathit{puk} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{pun} \leq \mathit{puk}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pux} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \lvert (\operatorname{ffam}(\mathit{puk})(\mathit{pux}) - f(\mathit{pux})) \rvert \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \leq\; \mathit{eps} \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{puk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{gfam}(\mathit{puk})(a) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{pug}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}primitive}(\mathit{pug}, f, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{pux} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, (\lambda \mathit{puk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{gfam}(\mathit{puk})(\mathit{pux})), \operatorname{pug}(\mathit{pux})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivative-family-uniform-limit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{fam}, \mathit{phifam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})), \psi \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (a < b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(\operatorname{fam}(k), \operatorname{phifam}(k), a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{fam}(k)(a) = 0) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{eps}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists n \in \mathbb{N}. \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (n \leq k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lvert (\psi(x) - \operatorname{phifam}(k)(x)) \rvert \leq \mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists f \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivative}(f, \psi, a, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{eps}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists n \in \mathbb{N}. \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (n \leq k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lvert (f(x) - \operatorname{fam}(k)(x)) \rvert \leq \mathit{eps}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{antiderivable-uniform-limit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{phifam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})), \psi \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\operatorname{phifam}(k), a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{eps}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists n \in \mathbb{N}. \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (n \leq k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lvert (\psi(x) - \operatorname{phifam}(k)(x)) \rvert \leq \mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\psi, a, b) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-at-ptwise-limit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{fam}, \mathit{phifam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})), f, \varphi \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), t, \rho \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \rho) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \varphi, t) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}, y \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad (\lvert (y - t) \rvert \leq \rho) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{fam}(k)(y) - \operatorname{fam}(k)(t)) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{phifam}(k)(y) \cdot (y - t)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall y \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad (\lvert (y - t) \rvert \leq \rho) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, (\lambda \operatorname{k\_} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{fam}(\operatorname{k\_})(y)), f(y)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall y \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad (\lvert (y - t) \rvert \leq \rho) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{converges\text{-}to}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, (\lambda \operatorname{k\_} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{phifam}(\operatorname{k\_})(y)), \varphi(y)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}at}(f, t, \varphi(t)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-23 (batch 22): primitive-uniform-limit is Dieudonne (8.6.4) on [a, b] with COUNTABLE exceptional sets -- g\_k a primitive of f\_k, the f\_k uniformly convergent to f on [a, b], g\_k(a) = 0 -- concluding a primitive of f to which the g\_k converge; it is still the NORMALISED form (g\_k(a) = 0 rather than the notes' convergent f\_k(a)), hence partial. EARLIER NOTE: The library version NORMALISES the sequence: it demands fam(k)(a) = 0 for EVERY k, where the notes assume only that \{f\_k(a)\} is convergent, so the notes' hypothesis (2) is replaced by a stronger and non-equivalent one. Hypothesis (1) is replaced too: instead of f\_k' being defined and CONTINUOUS on [a,b], the library assumes is-antiderivative(fam(k), phifam(k), a, b), which gives differentiability only on the OPEN interval (a,b) and says nothing about continuity of phifam(k). Of the four conclusions of the notes, it delivers the existence of f = lim f\_k (as a uniform limit on ccint(a, b)) and is-antiderivative(f, psi, a, b); it does NOT state that psi is continuous, does not state that f is differentiable at the ENDPOINTS (the notes explicitly extend the conclusion to them via one-sided derivatives), and does not state f\_k' --$>$ f' uniformly. All functions are in fun(rr, rr), TOTAL on RR, uniform convergence is written inline over ccint(a, b), and a $<$ b is strict.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{4.17}
\begin{cor}[{The antiderivable functions are closed under uniform limits}]\label{thm:antiderivable-uniform-limit}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{phifam} \in (\mathbb{N} \to (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R})), \psi \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), a, b \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\operatorname{phifam}(k), a, b) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{eps}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists n \in \mathbb{N}. \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (n \leq k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall x \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (x \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lvert (\psi(x) - \operatorname{phifam}(k)(x)) \rvert \leq \mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}antiderivable}(\psi, a, b) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (19 steps; 7 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact antiderivable-family-normalized, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact nn-zero-in, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(inst+ 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact antiderivative-endpoints, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact antiderivative-family-uniform-limit, 6 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac is-antiderivable, 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ew 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{antiderivable-family-normalized}, \texttt{nn-zero-in}, \texttt{antiderivative-endpoints}, \texttt{antiderivative-family-uniform-limit}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{crs}, \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Uniform convergence is spelled out inline (for every eps $>$ 0 there is n\_ in nn with abs(psi(x\_) - (phifam(k\_))(x\_)) $<$= eps for all k\_ $>$= n\_ and all x\_ in ccint(a, b)) rather than through a named predicate, and is required only on ccint(a, b). The sequence and its limit are in fun(rr, rr), TOTAL on RR, and a $<$ b is strict, so the degenerate interval is excluded.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.2}
\begin{thm}[{Bernstein approximation of a continuous function on [0,1]}]\label{thm:bernstein-uniform-approximation}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \varphi \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), \mathit{eps}. \\ \quad \forall x \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \varphi, x) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{eps}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{cap} \in \mathbb{N}. \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, \operatorname{x\_}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{cap} \leq n) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{x\_} \in \operatorname{ccint}(0, 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \lvert (\varphi(\operatorname{x\_}) - \operatorname{bernstein\text{-}poly}(\varphi, n, \operatorname{x\_})) \rvert \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \leq\; \mathit{eps} \end{array}}
%
\end{thm}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} f is required to be in fun(rr, rr), i.e. TOTAL on RR, with continuity assumed only at the points of ccint(0, 1) and there TWO-SIDED, including at 0 and at 1; the notes have f continuous on [0,1]. The conclusion is given as a single eps/N estimate -- eps is a PARAMETER of the theorem and the claim is forsome cap\_ in nn, for all n\_ $>$= cap\_ and all x\_ in ccint(0,1), abs(f\_(x\_) - bernstein-poly(f\_, n\_, x\_)) $<$= eps\_ -- rather than as the statement that f is the uniform limit of the sequence B\_n. bernstein-poly(f, n, x) is the functoid series-partial-sum(l\_ |--$>$ f(l\_/n) * (bernstein-basis(n,x))(l\_), succ(n)), so the notes' sum from 0 to n appears as a partial sum of length n+1.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.4}
\begin{prop}[{The two Bernstein estimates}]\label{thm:bernstein-partition}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{bernstein-partition}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, x \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}(\operatorname{bernstein\text{-}basis}(n, x), (n + 1)) \\ \quad =\; 1 \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bernstein-variance-bound}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, x, h. \\ \quad \neg (n = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (x \in \mathbb{R}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad h(k) \\ \quad \quad =\; (((k - (n \cdot x)) \cdot (k - (n \cdot x))) \cdot \operatorname{bernstein\text{-}basis}(n, x)(k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad ((/(1, n) \cdot \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}(h, (n + 1))) \leq 1) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Both identities are stated with series-partial-sum(..., succ(n)) in place of the notes' sum from l = 0 to n, and bernstein-basis(n, x) is a function on ZZ (bernstein-basis-in-fun), so the out-of-range terms are zero by the separate bernstein-basis-above and bernstein-basis-null rather than by the range of the sum. The second estimate's summand cannot be written inline: it must be supplied as an auxiliary sequence h\_ pinned pointwise by forall k\_ in nn, h\_(k\_) = ((k\_ - n\_ x\_)\textasciicircum{}2) (bernstein-basis(n\_, x\_))(k\_). bernstein-variance-bound additionally requires n\_ /= 0, which the notes leave implicit in the factor 1/n.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.5}
\begin{lem}[{The four Bernstein identities}]\label{thm:calculus-5.5}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{bernstein-partition}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, x \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}(\operatorname{bernstein\text{-}basis}(n, x), (n + 1)) \\ \quad =\; 1 \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bernstein-moment-1}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, x \in \mathbb{R}, h. \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (h(k) = (k \cdot \operatorname{bernstein\text{-}basis}(n, x)(k))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}(h, (n + 1)) = (n \cdot x)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bernstein-moment-2}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, x \in \mathbb{R}, h. \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (h(k) = ((k \cdot (k - 1)) \cdot \operatorname{bernstein\text{-}basis}(n, x)(k))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}(h, (n + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; ((n \cdot (n - 1)) \cdot (x \cdot x)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{bernstein-variance}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, x \in \mathbb{R}, h. \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad h(k) \\ \quad \quad =\; (((k - (n \cdot x)) \cdot (k - (n \cdot x))) \cdot \operatorname{bernstein\text{-}basis}(n, x)(k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{series\text{-}partial\text{-}sum}(h, (n + 1)) = ((n \cdot x) \cdot (1 - x))) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Each of the last three identities is stated through an auxiliary sequence h\_ pinned pointwise (forall k\_ in nn, h\_(k\_) = ...) and the sum is series-partial-sum(h\_, succ(n\_)), because the library has no inline finite-sum term with a bound variable; bernstein-basis(n, x) is a function on ZZ, so the range of the notes' sum is enforced by bernstein-basis-above and bernstein-basis-null rather than by the summation. The notes derive the identities from the Binomial Theorem by differentiating in x; the library's route is bernstein-basis-succ and induction, so the proof does not follow the notes (binomial-theorem exists independently).
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{5.7}
\begin{cor}[{Weierstrass approximation on an arbitrary interval}]\label{thm:bernstein-uniform-approximation-ccint}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{fn} \in (\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}), a, b, \mathit{ep}. \\ \quad ((a \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((b \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge (a < b))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \operatorname{x\_} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}continuous\text{-}at}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, \mathit{fn}, \operatorname{x\_}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{ep}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{cap} \in \mathbb{N}. \forall n. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((n \in \mathbb{N}) \wedge (\mathit{cap} \leq n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \operatorname{x\_} \in \operatorname{ccint}(a, b). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \lvert (\operatorname{fn}(\operatorname{x\_}) - \operatorname{bernstein\text{-}poly}(\operatorname{compose}(\mathit{fn}, (\lambda x \in \mathbb{R}.\; (a + ((b - a) \cdot x)))), n, ((\operatorname{x\_} - a) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((b - a))))) \rvert \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \leq\; \mathit{ep} \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The library exhibits ONE SPECIFIC approximant -- the transported Bernstein polynomial bernstein-poly(compose(fn\_, x |--$>$ a + (b-a)*x), n\_, (x\_ - a) * recip(b - a)) -- and bounds abs(fn\_(x\_) - that) by eps. It never says that this term IS a polynomial, and there is no statement anywhere of the form the notes make, that any continuous function on [a,b] is a uniform limit of a sequence of POLYNOMIALS: there is no predicate for being a polynomial function on RR to connect the two. Further: fn\_ in fun(rr, rr), TOTAL on RR; continuity assumed two-sided at every x\_ in ccint(a, b); a $<$ b strictly, so the degenerate interval is excluded; and eps is a parameter with the claim in eps/N form rather than the notes' uniform-limit form.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.3}
\begin{lem}[{Action of the matrix unit E\_n[k,l] on the right}]\label{thm:matunit-col-shift}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall m, n, p \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)), k, l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m), c \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\operatorname{matmul}(a, p, \operatorname{matunit}(a, n, k, l)), i, c) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; \left(\text{if }(c = l)\text{ then }\operatorname{entry}(p, i, k)\text{ else }\operatorname{zero}(a)\right) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Generality GAINED: the library proves it over an arbitrary ring (is-ring), while the notes' section fixes R commutative.  The library states the conclusion entrywise -- entry(matmul(a,p,matunit(a,n,k,l)),i,c) = if(c = l, entry(p,i,k), zero(a)) -- where the notes name the resulting matrix A'; same content. \renewcommand{\thethm}{3.5}
\begin{prop}[{The elementary column operations}]\label{thm:elem-f-action}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-f-action}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall m, n, p \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)), k, l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m), c \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\operatorname{matmul}(a, p, \operatorname{elem\text{-}f}(a, n, k, l)), i, c) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \left(\text{if }(c = k)\text{ then }\operatorname{entry}(p, i, l)\text{ else }\left(\text{if }(c = l)\text{ then }\operatorname{entry}(p, i, k)\text{ else }\operatorname{entry}(p, i, c)\right)\right) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-g-action}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall m, n, p \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)), r \in \operatorname{carr}(a), k, l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m), c \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\operatorname{matmul}(a, p, \operatorname{elem\text{-}g}(a, n, r, k, l)), i, c) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \left(\text{if }(c = l)\text{ then }\operatorname{add}(a)(\operatorname{entry}(p, i, l), \operatorname{mul}(a)(\operatorname{entry}(p, i, k), r))\text{ else }\operatorname{entry}(p, i, c)\right) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-h-action}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall m, n, p \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)), r \in \operatorname{carr}(a), k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m), c \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\operatorname{matmul}(a, p, \operatorname{elem\text{-}h}(a, n, r, k)), i, c) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; \left(\text{if }(c = k)\text{ then }\operatorname{mul}(a)(\operatorname{entry}(p, i, k), r)\text{ else }\operatorname{entry}(p, i, c)\right) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Generality GAINED: stated over an arbitrary ring (is-ring), not a commutative ring, and elem-h-action asks only r in carr(a), NOT that r be invertible (the notes build invertibility of r into the definition of H).  Split into three entrywise theorems on matmul(a,p,elem-x(...)) instead of one prose sentence; elem-f-action and elem-g-action carry the notes' own k /= l guard.  The row-operation mirrors (elem-f-row-action, elem-g-row-action, elem-h-row-action) are proven as well, which the notes only define by transposition.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.6}
\begin{cor}[{The elementary column matrices are invertible, with explicit inverses}]\label{thm:elem-f-inverse}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-f-inverse}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, k, l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{matmul}(a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}f}(a, n, k, l), \operatorname{elem\text{-}f}(a, n, l, k)) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{identmat}(a, n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-g-inverse}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, r \in \operatorname{carr}(a), k, l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{matmul}(a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}g}(a, n, r, k, l), \operatorname{elem\text{-}g}(a, n, \operatorname{neg}(a)(r), k, l)) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{identmat}(a, n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-h-inverse}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, r, s \in \operatorname{carr}(a), k. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{mul}(a)(r, s) = \operatorname{one}(a)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{matmul}(a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}h}(a, n, r, k), \operatorname{elem\text{-}h}(a, n, s, k)) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{identmat}(a, n) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-f-invertible}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, k, l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(a, n, \operatorname{elem\text{-}f}(a, n, k, l)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{elem-g-invertible}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}, r \in \operatorname{carr}(a), k, l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(a, n, \operatorname{elem\text{-}g}(a, n, r, k, l)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Two differences.  (1) F and G are given is-invertible-mat (elem-f-invertible, elem-g-invertible), but there is NO elem-h-invertible: for H the library installs only the product equation matmul(a,elem-h(a,n,r,k),elem-h(a,n,s,k)) = identmat(a,n) under the hypothesis mul(a)(r,s) = one(a), so the inverse is a SUPPLIED s, not r\textasciicircum{}\{-1\} -- the library has no ring-inverse operation.  (2) Generality gained: is-ring rather than a commutative ring.  The notes' G inverse formula G[-r,k,l] and the k /= l guard match elem-g-inverse exactly.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.8}
\begin{lem}[{Column reduction of the first row over a field}]\label{thm:clear-first-row}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{clear-first-row}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall m, n \in \mathbb{N}, p \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)). \\ \quad \quad \quad (1 \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (1 \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (\operatorname{entry}(p, 1, 1) = \operatorname{zero}(a)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}equiv}(a, m, n, p, c) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ii} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m), \mathit{jj} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (\operatorname{entry}(c, \mathit{ii}, \mathit{jj}) = \operatorname{zero}(a)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{gauge}(a)(\operatorname{entry}(p, 1, 1)) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{gauge}(a)(\operatorname{entry}(c, \mathit{ii}, \mathit{jj})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists q. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}equiv}(a, m, n, p, q) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(q, 1, 1) = \operatorname{entry}(p, 1, 1)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (j = 1) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(q, 1, j) = \operatorname{zero}(a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{class-min-pivot}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall m, n, p \in \operatorname{mat}(m, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)). \\ \quad \quad \quad (1 \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (1 \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \exists i_{0} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m), j_{0} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (\operatorname{entry}(p, i_{0}, j_{0}) = \operatorname{zero}(a)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists b. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}equiv}(a, m, n, p, b) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (\operatorname{entry}(b, 1, 1) = \operatorname{zero}(a)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall c. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}equiv}(a, m, n, p, c) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, m), j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (\operatorname{entry}(c, i, j) = \operatorname{zero}(a)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{gauge}(a)(\operatorname{entry}(b, 1, 1)) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \leq\; \operatorname{gauge}(a)(\operatorname{entry}(c, i, j)) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Three losses and one gain.  The library works over a EUCLIDEAN RING, not a field (gain), and therefore (a) cannot scale the pivot: clear-first-row concludes entry(q,1,1) = entry(p,1,1) and never normalises the corner to 0 or 1, which is precisely the notes' conclusion b\_11 in \{0,1\}; (b) needs the pivot to be nonzero AND to MINIMISE the gauge over the whole equivalence class (that hypothesis is supplied by class-min-pivot), where the notes need no such thing; (c) works modulo MAT-EQUIV, which is two-sided (an invertible U on the left and V on the right), not the notes' column equivalence.  Extra guards: m, n in nn and 1 in interval(1,m), 1 in interval(1,n).

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Neither statement implies the other.  smith-diagonalization reaches a FULLY DIAGONAL d (is-diagonal: every off-diagonal entry zero) over a euclidean ring, which is stronger than the notes' zeros above the diagonal; but it reaches it through MAT-EQUIV -- row AND column operations -- where the notes use COLUMN operations only, and it does not normalise the diagonal entries to 0 or 1 (that step needs a field).  The library has no column-only equivalence relation at all.

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The library has the monoid algebra monalg(a,m) and, on top of it, poly(a) = monalg over the additive monoid of NN, i.e. ONE-VARIABLE polynomials only; there is no R[x\_1,...,x\_n].  permutations(n) is defined (injection(ord-segment(n), ord-segment(n))) but acts on nothing.  No sign of a permutation, hence none of the sign machinery under this proposition either.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.18}
\begin{prop}[{det is multilinear and alternating, and det of the transpose equals det}]\label{thm:det-row-linear}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-row-linear}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, b, c, p, \mathit{sc}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (b \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (c \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sc} \in \operatorname{carr}(r)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dri} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dri} = p) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dri} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dri} = p) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(c, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(c, p, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{add}(r)(\operatorname{mul}(r)(\mathit{sc}, \operatorname{entry}(a, p, \mathit{drk})), \operatorname{entry}(b, p, \mathit{drk})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, c) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{add}(r)(\operatorname{mul}(r)(\mathit{sc}, \operatorname{det}(r, n, a)), \operatorname{det}(r, n, b)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-col-linear}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, b, c, p, \mathit{sc}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (b \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (c \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sc} \in \operatorname{carr}(r)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dcj} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dcj} = p) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{dci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{dci}, \mathit{dcj}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, \mathit{dcj}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dcj} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dcj} = p) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{dci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(c, \mathit{dci}, \mathit{dcj}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, \mathit{dcj}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(c, \mathit{dci}, p) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{add}(r)(\operatorname{mul}(r)(\mathit{sc}, \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, p)), \operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{dci}, p)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, c) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{add}(r)(\operatorname{mul}(r)(\mathit{sc}, \operatorname{det}(r, n, a)), \operatorname{det}(r, n, b)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-swap-rows}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, b, p, q. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (b \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (q \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (p = q) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dri} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dri} = p) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dri} = q) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(b, p, \mathit{drk}) = \operatorname{entry}(a, q, \mathit{drk})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(b, q, \mathit{drk}) = \operatorname{entry}(a, p, \mathit{drk})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{det}(r, n, b) = \operatorname{neg}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-swap-cols}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, b, p, q. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (b \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (q \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (p = q) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dcj} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dcj} = p) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dcj} = q) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{dci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{dci}, \mathit{dcj}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, \mathit{dcj}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{dci}, p) = \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, q)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(b, \mathit{dci}, q) = \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, p)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{det}(r, n, b) = \operatorname{neg}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-alternating-rows}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, p, q. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (q \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (p = q) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(a, p, k) = \operatorname{entry}(a, q, k)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{det}(r, n, a) = \operatorname{zero}(r)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-equal-cols-zero}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, p, q. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (q \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (p = q) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dci} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, p) = \operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dci}, q)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{det}(r, n, a) = \operatorname{zero}(r)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-transpose}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{transpose}(a, n, n)) = \operatorname{det}(r, n, a)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-25 (batch 32): PROVEN in full over any commutative ring: TRANSPOSE is defined entrywise (structure-library/transpose.scm, the user's decision), det-col-linear, det-swap-cols and det-equal-cols-zero are the column clauses, and det-transpose (det(A\textasciicircum{}t) = det A) follows from the uniqueness theorem det-alternating-form since X |-$>$ det(X\textasciicircum{}t) is alternating n-linear in the rows. UPDATED 2026-09-24 (batch 25): the ROW clauses are PROVEN over any commutative ring (theorem-library/det-rows.scm): det-row-linear (linear in each row), det-swap-rows (interchanging two rows negates det), and det-alternating-rows (two equal rows give 0) is now a THEOREM, its support retired; the proof from the first-row cofactor definition needs a second level of expansion (rows 1 and 2 equal: a double sum cancelling in pairs, no division by 2, so characteristic 2 is covered). The COLUMN clauses and det(A\textasciicircum{}t) = det A wait on a TRANSPOSE, which is a definition (proposed in BATCH25-REPORTS.md, not added). EARLIER NOTE: Only one of the three claims exists, and in a different form.  det-alternating-rows is ASSERTED (warrant reference) and says that two EQUAL rows force det = zero(r) -- not that interchanging two rows changes the sign.  Linearity in each row and in each column is absent.  det(A\textasciicircum{}t) = det(A) is absent and unstatable: the library has NO matrix transpose operation.  Ring hypothesis agrees (is-commutative-ring).  Note that the library's det is DEFINED by cofactor expansion along the first row, not by the notes' sum over permutations, so even the definitions are only provably equal in principle.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.19}
\begin{cor}[{Determinant under an elementary column operation}]\label{thm:det-elem-f-col}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-elem-f-col}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, k, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}f}(r, n, k, l))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{neg}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-elem-g-col}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, \mathit{sc}, k, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sc} \in \operatorname{carr}(r)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}g}(r, n, \mathit{sc}, k, l))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{det}(r, n, a) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-elem-h-col}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, \mathit{sc}, k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sc} \in \operatorname{carr}(r)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}h}(r, n, \mathit{sc}, k))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\mathit{sc}, \operatorname{det}(r, n, a)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-mul-elem-f-col}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, k, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}f}(r, n, k, l))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a), \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{elem\text{-}f}(r, n, k, l))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-mul-elem-g-col}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, \mathit{sc}, k, l. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sc} \in \operatorname{carr}(r)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (l \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \neg (k = l) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}g}(r, n, \mathit{sc}, k, l))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a), \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{elem\text{-}g}(r, n, \mathit{sc}, k, l))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-mul-elem-h-col}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, \mathit{sc}, k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sc} \in \operatorname{carr}(r)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (k \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, a, \operatorname{elem\text{-}h}(r, n, \mathit{sc}, k))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a), \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{elem\text{-}h}(r, n, \mathit{sc}, k))) \end{array}}

\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.20}
\begin{cor}[{det(AV) = det A det V for invertible V over a field}]\label{thm:det-mul-invertible}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-mul-invertible}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, v. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}field\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(r, n, v) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, a, v)) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a), \operatorname{det}(r, n, v)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-multiplicative}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, p, q. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (q \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, p, q)) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, p), \operatorname{det}(r, n, q)) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{det-mul-invertible}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (15 steps; 7 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(cut 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(mac-h is-field-ring-def, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ai 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact invertible-mat-is-mat, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact det-multiplicative, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}

%

%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.22}
\begin{prop}[{Expansion by minors along a row and along a column}]\label{thm:det-expand-row}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-expand-row}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, i. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}((n + 1), (n + 1), \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (i \in \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, (n + 1), a) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{finsum}(\operatorname{ring\text{-}additive\text{-}ag}(r), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{dxj} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1)).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{mpow}(\operatorname{ring\text{-}multiplicative\text{-}monoid}(r), \operatorname{neg}(r)(\operatorname{one}(r)), (i + \mathit{dxj})), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{entry}(a, i, \mathit{dxj}), \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{minor}(a, i, \mathit{dxj}, n))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-expand-col}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a, j. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}((n + 1), (n + 1), \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, (n + 1), a) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{finsum}(\operatorname{ring\text{-}additive\text{-}ag}(r), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{dce} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1)).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{mpow}(\operatorname{ring\text{-}multiplicative\text{-}monoid}(r), \operatorname{neg}(r)(\operatorname{one}(r)), (\mathit{dce} + j)), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{entry}(a, \mathit{dce}, j), \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{minor}(a, \mathit{dce}, j, n))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-cofactor}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}((n + 1), (n + 1), \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{det}(r, (n + 1), a) \simeq \operatorname{finsum}(\operatorname{ring\text{-}additive\text{-}ag}(r), (\lambda j \in \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1)).\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{mpow}(\operatorname{ring\text{-}multiplicative\text{-}monoid}(r), \operatorname{neg}(r)(\operatorname{one}(r)), (j + 1)), \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{entry}(a, 1, j), \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{minor}(a, 1, j, n))))), \operatorname{interval}(1, (n + 1)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{det-expand-row}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (10 steps; 3 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact interval-elt-in-nn, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact interval-lo, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact interval-hi, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact det-expand-row-ind, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}

\end{cor}
