\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.27}
\begin{prop}[{det is multiplicative}]\label{thm:det-multiplicative}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-multiplicative}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, p, q. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (p \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (q \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{det}(r, n, \operatorname{matmul}(r, p, q)) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, p), \operatorname{det}(r, n, q)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{det-alternating-form}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall r, n, d, a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}commutative\text{-}ring}(r) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (d \in (\operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r)) \to \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dfa}, \mathit{dfb}, \mathit{dfc} \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r)), \mathit{dfp} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n), \mathit{dfs} \in \operatorname{carr}(r). \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{dri} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dri} = \mathit{dfp}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfb}, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfa}, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{dri} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dri} = \mathit{dfp}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfc}, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfa}, \mathit{dri}, \mathit{drk}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfc}, \mathit{dfp}, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{add}(r)(\operatorname{mul}(r)(\mathit{dfs}, \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfa}, \mathit{dfp}, \mathit{drk})), \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfb}, \mathit{dfp}, \mathit{drk})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad d(\mathit{dfc}) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{add}(r)(\operatorname{mul}(r)(\mathit{dfs}, d(\mathit{dfa})), d(\mathit{dfb})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{dfa} \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r)), \mathit{dfp}, \mathit{dfq} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{dfp} = \mathit{dfq}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{drk} \in \operatorname{interval}(1, n). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfa}, \mathit{dfp}, \mathit{drk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{entry}(\mathit{dfa}, \mathit{dfq}, \mathit{drk}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad (d(\mathit{dfa}) = \operatorname{zero}(r)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad (a \in \operatorname{mat}(n, n, \operatorname{carr}(r))) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (d(a) = \operatorname{mul}(r)(\operatorname{det}(r, n, a), d(\operatorname{identmat}(r, n)))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{det-multiplicative}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (21 steps; 6 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact commutative-ring-is-ring, 2 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact identmat-type, 3 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact daf-det-rm-fun, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact daf-det-rm-lin, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact daf-det-rm-alt, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact det-alternating-form, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(lam-b-h 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(focus 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact identmat-left-identity, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact det-in-carrier, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact det-in-carrier, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact ring-carrier-closed-mul, 4 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(subst 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(subst 1 argument)}} \mbox{\texttt{(rfl)}}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{commutative-ring-is-ring}, \texttt{identmat-type}, \texttt{daf-det-rm-fun}, \texttt{daf-det-rm-lin}, \texttt{daf-det-rm-alt}, \texttt{det-alternating-form}, \texttt{identmat-left-identity}, \texttt{det-in-carrier}, \texttt{ring-carrier-closed-mul}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{arith}, \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{crs}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\vnbprf{\vnbproofpart{\texttt{det-alternating-form}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Tactics, in the order used} (9 steps; 3 distinct). {\small \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(di)}} \mbox{\texttt{(fact det-alternating-form-ind, 5 arguments)}} \mbox{\texttt{(ass)}}}}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Lemmas.} \texttt{det-alternating-form-ind}.}
%
\vnbprf{\textbf{Oracles.} \texttt{ineq}, \texttt{arith}, \texttt{crs}.  \textbf{Bill:} \texttt{proven modulo 0}.}
%
\end{proof}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.29}
\begin{prop}[{Behaviour of the sigma-th order subdeterminants under F and G operations}]\label{thm:linear-algebra-3.29}
%
\textit{If B comes from A by an F row or column operation then sdet\_sigma B = sdet\_sigma A up to sign; if by a G operation then every element of sdet\_sigma B has the form a + s a' with a, a' in sdet\_sigma A and s = 0 or s = +/- r.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The library has no submatrix obtained by deleting SEVERAL rows and columns (minor deletes exactly one of each; submat and block cut a leading or trailing rectangle), no set minor\_sigma A, and no sdet\_sigma A.  Nothing about how determinants of such minors move under elementary operations.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.31}
\begin{cor}[{The gcd of the sigma-th subdeterminants is an invariant over Z}]\label{thm:linear-algebra-3.31}
%
\textit{If A, B in M\_\{m x n\}(Z) and A -$>$ B by elementary F, G row and column operations over Z, then gcd sdet\_sigma A = +/- gcd sdet\_sigma B.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{cor}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Depends on 3.29, which is absent.  The library has zz-is-gcd and zz-bezout for a PAIR of integers, but no gcd of a set of integers and no subdeterminants.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.36}
\begin{prop}[{Integer normal form: existence and uniqueness of the diagonal form}]\label{thm:smith-normal-form}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{smith-normal-form}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall k, n \in \mathbb{N}, p \in \operatorname{mat}(k, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)). \exists d, \mathit{kk} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}equiv}(a, k, n, p, d) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{smith\text{-}staircase}(a, k, n, d, \mathit{kk}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{smith-diagonalization}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall k, n \in \mathbb{N}, p \in \operatorname{mat}(k, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)). \exists d. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}equiv}(a, k, n, p, d) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diagonal}(a, k, n, d) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The heaviest gap in the chapter.  smith-normal-form gives, over a EUCLIDEAN RING (Z qualifies, zz-is-euclidean-ring), the EXISTENCE of a mat-equiv d that is is-diagonal and whose nonzero diagonal entries form an initial segment of length kk (smith-staircase).  It does NOT give the divisibility chain b\_ii divides b\_jj, does NOT give non-negativity of the entries, and does NOT give UNIQUENESS -- the notes' whole second half.  Moreover the notes' relation \textasciitilde{} is generated by integral elementary operations, whereas mat-equiv is d = U c V for SOME invertible U, V; the two are never shown to coincide.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.37}
\begin{cor}[{The reducing matrices U and V are products of elementary matrices}]\label{thm:linear-algebra-3.37}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall a. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(a) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall k, n \in \mathbb{N}, p \in \operatorname{mat}(k, n, \operatorname{carr}(a)). \exists d, \mathit{kk} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mat\text{-}equiv}(a, k, n, p, d) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{smith\text{-}staircase}(a, k, n, d, \mathit{kk}) \end{array}}
%
\end{cor}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Unfolding mat-equiv inside smith-normal-form does produce invertible U (m x m) and V (n x n) with d = U A V, so part (1) holds as far as 3.36 goes.  Part (2) -- that U and V are PRODUCTS OF ELEMENTARY matrices -- is never established: mat-equiv is defined by existence of invertible factors, not by a sequence of elementary operations, and no theorem bridges the two.  The normal form reached also lacks 3.36's divisibility and non-negativity.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.38}
\begin{cor}[{An invertible integer matrix is a product of elementary matrices}]\label{thm:linear-algebra-3.38}
%
\textit{U in M\_m(Z) is invertible over Z if and only if it is a product U V with U a product of column elementary matrices and V a product of row elementary matrices.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.40}
\begin{lem}[{An invertible change of sequence preserves generation and freeness}]\label{thm:generates-transport}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{generates-transport}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{md}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(\mathit{md}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n, u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(\mathit{md})), \mathit{pm}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(\mathit{md}), n, \mathit{pm}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{generates}(\mathit{md}, n, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{generates}(\mathit{md}, n, \operatorname{matact}(\mathit{md}, \mathit{pm}, u)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{free-transport}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{md}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(\mathit{md}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall m, v \in \operatorname{mat}(m, 1, \operatorname{vec}(\mathit{md})), \mathit{qm}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(\mathit{md}), m, \mathit{qm}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(\mathit{md}, m, v) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(\mathit{md}, m, \operatorname{matact}(\mathit{md}, \mathit{qm}, v)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{spans-transport}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{md}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(\mathit{md}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n, u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(\mathit{md})), \mathit{pm}, \mathit{sm}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}invertible\text{-}mat}(\operatorname{scal}(\mathit{md}), n, \mathit{pm}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}submodule}(\mathit{md}, \mathit{sm}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{spans}(\mathit{md}, n, u, \mathit{sm}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{spans}(\mathit{md}, n, \operatorname{matact}(\mathit{md}, \mathit{pm}, u), \mathit{sm}) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The library's two statements are ONE-WAY implications, not the notes' iff: generates(md,n,u) implies generates(md,n,matact(md,pm,u)), and rel-free(md,m,v) implies rel-free(md,m,matact(md,qm,v)).  The converses (which follow by applying the same theorems to the inverse matrix) are not installed.  Setting: a module md over any ring with the transport matrix invertible over scal(md); the notes' E is an ABELIAN GROUP and U is over Z, and the library has NO abelian-group-as-ZZ-module view (zz-act exists as an integer action, but no module structure is built from it), so the notes' own case is not an instance of the library statement.  spans-transport is the submodule version, not in the notes.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.41}
\begin{prop}[{A relation-free sequence is no longer than a generating sequence}]\label{thm:free-length-le-generators}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{md}. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}module}(\mathit{md}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}euclidean\text{-}ring}(\operatorname{scal}(\mathit{md})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall n, m \in \mathbb{N}, u \in \operatorname{mat}(n, 1, \operatorname{vec}(\mathit{md})), v \in \operatorname{mat}(m, 1, \operatorname{vec}(\mathit{md})). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{generates}(\mathit{md}, n, u) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{rel\text{-}free}(\mathit{md}, m, v) \Rightarrow (m \leq n)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

The second sentence -- that all free generating sequences of an abelian group have the same LENGTH, the fact that makes rank well defined -- is NOT stated anywhere, although it follows by two applications of the first.  Guards the notes do not carry: n, m in nn, and both sequences are column matrices u in mat(n,1,vec(md)), v in mat(m,1,vec(md)).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{3.43}
\begin{cor}[{GL\_n(Z) acts freely and transitively on the free generating sequences}]\label{thm:linear-algebra-3.43}
%
\textit{If E is a free abelian group of rank n, the action (A, u) |-$>$ A . u of M\_n\textasciicircum{}x(Z) on free generating sequences of E is free and transitive.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.7}
\begin{prop}[{Monotone convergence for real sequences}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.7}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\; (f(k) \leq f((k + 1))) \wedge \\ \quad \exists \mathit{bnd} \in \mathbb{R}. \forall k \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (f(k) \leq \mathit{bnd}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{converges}(\operatorname{rr\text{-}ms}, f) \end{array}}

\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.9}
\begin{prop}[{Closed sets and limits of sequences}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.9}

\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.11}

%

\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-iff-cluster-point}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow \forall f \in (\mathbb{N} \to \operatorname{pts}(s)).\; \exists x.\; \operatorname{cluster\text{-}point}(s, f, x)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{compact-iff-tb-complete}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall s. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}metric\text{-}space}(s) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{is\text{-}compact}(s) \Leftrightarrow (\operatorname{totally\text{-}bounded}(s) \wedge \operatorname{is\text{-}complete}(s))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

(3) is stated with CLUSTER-POINT defined by: for every eps $>$ 0 and every m in NN there is n $>$= m with dist(f(n), x) $<$ eps -- the notes define a cluster point by the set \{n : x\_n in B(y,r)\} being infinite.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.15}
\begin{thm}[{C is an algebraically closed field}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.15}
%
\textit{C is an algebraically closed field: every polynomial equation a\_n z\textasciicircum{}n + ... + a\_0 = 0 with n $>$= 1 and a\_n /= 0 has a solution in C.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{thm}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Nothing about roots of polynomials over CC. The library has no polynomial with complex coefficients as a function on CC, no n-th roots of a complex number, and no statement that a non-constant polynomial has a zero. The nearest facts are the algebraic ones about CC: cc-is-normed-field (proven) -- note that IS-NORMED-FIELD has no MUL-INV slot and does NOT require multiplicative inverses, so it is not the field property -- together with the flat CC arithmetic axioms cc-recip-closed and cc-recip-inverse, which do supply inverses of non-zero complex numbers.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{1.16}
\begin{lem}[{Convergence in the extended plane}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-1.16}
%
\textit{For a sequence \{x\_n\} in C: it converges to x in C in the topology of C-hat iff it converges to x in the Euclidean metric; it converges to infinity iff |x\_n| -$>$ +infinity.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%
\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}
%
\end{proof}
%
\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The library has no one-point compactification of C: no C-hat, no topology on C union \{infinity\}, no |x\_n| -$>$ +infinity. Only convergence in the Euclidean metric space CC-MS is available (converges-to(cc-ms, f, l), with cc-converges-iff-coords and cc-complete), which is exactly the first half of the notes' `if and only if' but not the statement about the extended topology. %

%
Not in the library.

\end{prop}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.3}
\begin{prop}[{Sum and product rules}]\label{thm:diff-on-sum}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2m}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{d2x} \in u.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{add}(k)(\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2x}), \operatorname{d2g}(\mathit{d2x}))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{d2a}, \operatorname{add}(k)(\mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{diff-on-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2m}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{d2x} \in u.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{mul}(k)(\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2x}), \operatorname{d2g}(\mathit{d2x}))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{d2a}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{add}(k)(\operatorname{mul}(k)(\mathit{d2l}, \operatorname{d2g}(\mathit{d2a})), \operatorname{mul}(k)(\mathit{d2m}, \operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2a})))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{holomorphic-sum}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, f, g, \mathit{sm}. \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, f) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, g) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sm} \in (u \to \mathbb{C})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{hbx} \in u. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{sm}(\mathit{hbx}) \simeq (f(\mathit{hbx}) + g(\mathit{hbx}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, \mathit{sm}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{holomorphic-product}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall u, f, g, \mathit{sm}. \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, f) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, g) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{sm} \in (u \to \mathbb{C})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{hbx} \in u. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{sm}(\mathit{hbx}) \simeq (f(\mathit{hbx}) \cdot g(\mathit{hbx}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(u, \mathit{sm}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} Two separate developments, neither of which is exactly the notes' statement. diff-on-sum / diff-on-product give the derivative at a, but only for the LITERAL function VNB-LAMBDA x in U. (add K)(f(x), g(x)) (resp. the product); a pointwise-equal representative of f + g or f . g has to be transported by diff-on-transfer-ptwise-eq. holomorphic-sum / holomorphic-product do take an arbitrary sm in FUN(U, CC) that agrees pointwise, but they conclude only HOLOMORPHIC-ON(U, sm) and say nothing about the value of the derivative at a. Both diff-on laws are stated for a general normed field K.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.4}
\begin{prop}[{Chain Rule}]\label{thm:diff-on-chain}
%
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall k. \\ \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}normed\text{-}field}(k) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall u, \mathit{d2s}, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2g}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}, \mathit{d2m}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, \mathit{d2f}, \mathit{d2a}, \mathit{d2l}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, \mathit{d2s}, \mathit{d2g}, \operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2a}), \mathit{d2m}) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{d2y} \in u.\; (\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2y}) \in \mathit{d2s}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(k, u, (\lambda \mathit{d2x} \in u.\; \operatorname{d2g}(\operatorname{d2f}(\mathit{d2x}))), \mathit{d2a}, \operatorname{mul}(k)(\mathit{d2m}, \mathit{d2l})) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} The library adds hypotheses the notes leave implicit: both U and the target set S must be open (carried by IS-DIFF-ON), and forall y in U. f(y) in S is an explicit antecedent (the notes only require g to be differentiable at f(a)). The composite is the literal VNB-LAMBDA x in U. g(f(x)), so a pointwise-equal representative needs diff-on-transfer-ptwise-eq; the derivative is written (mul K)(m, l) in the normed field K. Stated for a general K, not specialised to CC.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.5}
\begin{lem}[{Root Test}]\label{thm:root-test-converges}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{root-test-converges}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cpsth} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (0 \leq \operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsk})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda \mathit{cpsj} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad {\operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsj})}^{{\mathit{cpsj}}^{\ast\!-1}})) \\ \quad <\; 1 \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{series\text{-}converges}(\mathit{cpsth}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{root-test-diverges}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cpsth} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (0 \leq \operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsk})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad 1 \\ \quad <\; \operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda \mathit{cpsj} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad {\operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsj})}^{{\mathit{cpsj}}^{\ast\!-1}})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{series\text{-}converges}(\mathit{cpsth}) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}
%
The proof uses the following tactics and lemmas.
%

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.10}
\begin{prop}[{A power series is holomorphic and differentiates termwise}]\label{thm:cps-holomorphic-ball}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-holomorphic-ball}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), \mathit{cpdr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{cpdr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{cpdr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk})))))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}((\lambda \mathit{cpdn} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad ((\mathit{cpdn} + 1) \cdot \operatorname{cf}((\mathit{cpdn} + 1))))) \\ \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{cpda} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk}))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{cpda}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (((\mathit{cpsk} + 1) \cdot \operatorname{cf}((\mathit{cpsk} + 1))) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpda}, \mathit{cpsk}))))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-radius-derived}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf}, \mathit{dcf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cpdj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{dcf}(\mathit{cpdj}) \\ \quad \quad =\; ((\mathit{cpdj} + 1) \cdot \operatorname{cf}((\mathit{cpdj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{dcf}) = \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-diff-on-ball}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf}, \mathit{dcf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cpdj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{dcf}(\mathit{cpdj}) \\ \quad \quad =\; ((\mathit{cpdj} + 1) \cdot \operatorname{cf}((\mathit{cpdj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{cpdr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{cpdr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{cpdr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{cpda} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk}))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{cpda}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{dcf}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpda}, \mathit{cpsk}))))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-24 (batch 26-A, theorem-library/cc-power-series-deriv.scm): PROVEN with one convention -- the library has no ball of radius +inf, so the statement is made on B(0, r) for every real 0 $<$ r $<$ R (which covers B(0, R) for finite R and CC for R = +inf): f is holomorphic on B(0, r), the derived series sum (k+1) a\_(k+1) z\textasciicircum{}k has the same radius, and f'(u) is its sum. The proof avoids the notes' double sum and lim n\textasciicircum{}(1/n) = 1 (absent): a one-step recurrence gives the second-order estimate, a radius-comparison lemma and Lemma 2.9 with b\_k = k give the radius. EARLIER NOTE: Nothing near, in either the complex or the real case. The library's power series are real and pointwise (PS-CONVERGES-AT); it has no theorem that the sum function of a power series is differentiable, no termwise-differentiated series, and no statement that the two series share a radius. HOLOMORPHIC-ON is available (holomorphic-basics.scm) but the only holomorphic functions exhibited are constants, the identity, powers, sums and products (holomorphic-const, holomorphic-identity, holomorphic-power, holomorphic-sum, holomorphic-product).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.12}
\begin{prop}[{Principle of Analytic Continuation}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-2.12}
%
\textit{Let U be a connected open set. If f is analytic in U and the set of zeros of f in U has an accumulation point in U, then f is identically 0 on U.}
%
Not in the library.
%
\end{prop}
%

\vnbprf{There is no library statement, and so no proof.}

\end{proof}

The library has no notion of an ANALYTIC function (no local power-series representation), and no connectedness of a subset of a metric space -- IS-CONNECTED does not exist in THEOREMS.md. Accumulation point is available only indirectly through CLOSURE / CLUSTER-POINT.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.13}
\begin{cor}[{Finitely many zeros in a closed ball}]\label{thm:complex-analysis-2.13}
%
\textit{Let U be a connected open set. If f is analytic in U and not identically 0, then f has only finitely many zeros within any closed ball B contained in U.}
%
Not in the library.

\end{cor}

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.14}
\begin{prop}[{Taylor coefficients of an analytic function}]\label{thm:taylor-coefficients-at}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-coefficients-at}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algf}, \mathit{algu}. \\ \quad (\mathit{algf} \in (\mathit{algu} \to \mathbb{C})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), \mathit{alga} \in \mathbb{C}, \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{algr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{algc})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \subseteq\; \mathit{algu} \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{algf}(\mathit{algz}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{algc}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{algz} - \mathit{alga}), \mathit{cpsk})))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algk} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{restrict}(\mathit{algf}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}))^{(\mathit{algk})}(\mathit{alga}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{algk}) \cdot \operatorname{algc}(\mathit{algk})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-coefficients}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), \mathit{cpdr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{cpdr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{cpdr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ndlk} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk})))))^{(\mathit{ndlk})}(0) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{ndlk}) \cdot \operatorname{cf}(\mathit{ndlk})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{taylor-coefficient-formula}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), \mathit{cpdr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{cpdr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{cpdr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ndlk} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cf}(\mathit{ndlk}) \\ \quad \quad \quad =\; ((\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk})))))^{(\mathit{ndlk})}(0) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{ndlk}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-translate-nth-deriv}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}), \mathit{alga} \in \mathbb{C}, \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{algr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{algc})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algk} \in \mathbb{N}, \mathit{algg} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{ctcn} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{algg}(\mathit{ctcn}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; ((\operatorname{factorial}((\mathit{ctcn} + \mathit{algk})) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{ctcn}))) \cdot \operatorname{algc}((\mathit{ctcn} + \mathit{algk}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{algc}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{algz} - \mathit{alga}), \mathit{cpsk})))))^{(\mathit{algk})} \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (\lambda \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{algg}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{algz} - \mathit{alga}), \mathit{cpsk}))))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{analytic-holomorphic-ball}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algf}, \mathit{algu}, \mathit{alga}. \\ \quad \mathit{algf} \text{ is analytic at } \mathit{alga} \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \subseteq\; \mathit{algu} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{restrict}(\mathit{algf}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{alga}, \mathit{algr}))) \end{array}}

((\operatorname{factorial}((\mathit{ctcn} + \mathit{ctck})) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{ctcn}))) \cdot \operatorname{cf}((\mathit{ctcn} + \mathit{ctck}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \forall \mathit{ctcn} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{ctch}(\mathit{ctcn}) \\ \quad \quad =\; ((\operatorname{factorial}((\mathit{ctcn} + (\mathit{ctck} + 1))) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{ctcn}))) \cdot \operatorname{cf}((\mathit{ctcn} + (\mathit{ctck} + 1)))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{cpdr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{cpdr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{cpdr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{ctcg}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk})))))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{ctcg}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk})))))(0) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{ctck}) \cdot \operatorname{cf}(\mathit{ctck})) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{cpda} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{deriv\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{ctcg}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk}))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{cpda}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{cpdr}).\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{ctch}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk})))))(\mathit{cpda}) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} PROVEN 2026-09-27 (batch 38) AT A CENTRE: IS-ANALYTIC-AT(f, U, a) is DEFINED (structure-library/analytic-log.scm, the notes' 2.11: U open, f in fun(U, cc), a power series of positive radius on a ball B(a, r) inside U), the power-series layer is translated from 0 to a (cps-translate-*), and taylor-coefficients-at states f\textasciicircum{}(k)(a) = k! a\_k with f\textasciicircum{}(k) the k-th NTH-DERIV-ON of f restricted to B(a, r). Earlier: UPDATED 2026-09-26 (batch 36): NTH-DERIV-ON(K, U, f, k) is DEFINED by NN-recursion (structure-library/nth-deriv.scm) and 2.14 is stated LITERALLY -- taylor-coefficients: the k-th derivative of the sum function at 0 is k! a\_k, for the power series at 0 on every ball B(0, r), r $<$ radius; taylor-coefficient-formula is the coefficient form. Still partial for one reason only: the notes' 'f analytic at a' (no IS-ANALYTIC predicate, no translation to a centre a). Earlier: Proven 2026-09-24 (batch 27-A) for a function GIVEN as a power series at 0 (the notes' proof reduces to this case by translation; the tree has no IS-ANALYTIC predicate, so the hypothesis 'f analytic at a' is not stated). The tree has no iterated derivative over CC: f\textasciicircum{}(k) is read as F\_k, the sum function of the k-th derived series, whose coefficients (n+k)!/n! a\_(n+k) are given by their values. For every real 0 $<$ r $<$ R: F\_k is holomorphic on B(0, r), DERIV-ON(F\_k) = F\_(k+1) on the ball, and F\_k(0) = k! a\_k; hence a\_k = F\_k(0)/k! (the second name).

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.15}
\begin{lem}[{Ratio Test}]\label{thm:ratio-test-converges-limsup}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{ratio-test-converges-limsup}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cpsth} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (0 < \operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsk})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \operatorname{elimsup}((\lambda \mathit{cpsj} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{cpsth}((\mathit{cpsj} + 1)) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsj}))))) \\ \quad <\; 1 \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{series\text{-}converges}(\mathit{cpsth}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{ratio-test-diverges-liminf}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cpsth} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (0 < \operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsk})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad 1 \\ \quad <\; \operatorname{eliminf}((\lambda \mathit{cpsj} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{cpsth}((\mathit{cpsj} + 1)) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{cpsth}(\mathit{cpsj}))))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \neg \operatorname{series\text{-}converges}(\mathit{cpsth}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{ratio-test-converges}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{coef} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}), l. \\ \quad (l \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ \quad (0 \leq l) \wedge \\ \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}.\; \neg (\operatorname{coef}(n) = 0) \wedge \\ \quad \operatorname{ps\text{-}ratio\text{-}limit}(\mathit{coef}, l) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall x. \\ \quad \quad \quad ((x \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge ((\lvert x \rvert \cdot l) < 1)) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{ps\text{-}converges\text{-}at}(\mathit{coef}, x) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%

THE SECOND HALF IS FALSE AS PRINTED: lim sup theta\_(k+1)/theta\_k $>$ 1 does not imply divergence (theta\_(2j) = 4\textasciicircum{}-j, theta\_(2j+1) = 2 * 4\textasciicircum{}-j has ratios alternating 2 and 1/8, lim sup 2, and sums to 4); the library states and proves the divergence half with lim INF $>$ 1. The older asserted ratio-test-converges (a real power series with a LIMIT of ratios) follows from the new one with two short bridges and remains asserted for now. EARLIER NOTE: A PSS entry (warrant: informal), not proven. The library's ratio test is not the notes' statement about a bare series of positive reals: it is about a REAL POWER SERIES, coef in FUN(NN, RR) with every coef(n) non-zero, and the ratio hypothesis is PS-RATIO-LIMIT(coef, l) -- the ratios |coef(n+1)/coef(n)| CONVERGE to l, a limit, not a lim sup -- with l in RR, 0 $<$= l; the conclusion is PS-CONVERGES-AT(coef, x) for every real x with |x| l $<$ 1. The divergence half (lim sup of the ratios $>$ 1 implies divergence) is absent.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.16}
\begin{lem}[{The exponential series has infinite radius}]\label{thm:cc-exp-radius}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-radius}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cek} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cek}) = \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(\mathit{cek}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf}) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-radius-pos-inf}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cext} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{cext}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{series\text{-}converges}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{magnitude}(\operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cpsk})) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cext}, \mathit{cpsk})))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf}) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-cos-radius}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cek} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cek}) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{cek}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}((2 \cdot \mathit{cek})))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf}) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-sin-radius}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cek} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{cf}(\mathit{cek}) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{cek}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}(\operatorname{factorial}(((2 \cdot \mathit{cek}) + 1)))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{cf}) = \operatorname{pos\text{-}inf}) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-25 (batch 31-A): PROVEN for the COMPLEX exponential defined by its series (theorem-library/cc-exp.scm): exp(z + w) = exp z exp w (cc-exp-add, by the zero-derivative route along a segment: exp(z) exp(w - z) is constant, no Cauchy product needed), exp 0 = 1, exp(-z) = 1/exp z, exp z /= 0, continuity and exp' = exp on CC. The tree has no group-homomorphism predicate, so 2.17 is these equations. The real exponential R-EXP (inverse of the integral LOG) is a separate object; the bridge 'exp restricted to RR is R-EXP' is not yet stated. There is no complex exponential in the library. R-EXP is the REAL exponential, and it is not defined by the power series: LOG is defined as the oriented integral of 1/x from 1 (log-unfold) and R-EXP is its inverse, so the identification of R-EXP with the restriction of the notes' exp is not a library fact. What is proven is the real restriction of the statement: r-exp-add (exp(u+v) = exp(u) exp(v) for real u, v), r-exp-pos (0 $<$ exp(y), i.e. the values land in the multiplicative group of the positive reals) and r-exp-continuous-at (continuity at each real point, in RR-MS). Nothing about C or C* = C minus \{0\}.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.18}
\begin{lem}[{The kernel of exp is 2 pi i Z}]\label{thm:cc-exp-one-iff}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-one-iff}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cekz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad ((\exp \mathit{cekz} = 1) \Leftrightarrow \exists \mathit{cekk} \in \mathbb{Z}.\; (\mathit{cekz} = (\mathit{cekk} \cdot ((2 \cdot \pi) \cdot +i)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{pi-spec}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} (\pi \in \mathbb{R}) \wedge \\ (0 < \pi) \wedge \\ \forall \mathit{cekz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad ((\exp \mathit{cekz} = 1) \Leftrightarrow \exists \mathit{cekk} \in \mathbb{Z}.\; (\mathit{cekz} = (\mathit{cekk} \cdot ((2 \cdot \pi) \cdot +i)))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-kernel-generator}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \exists \mathit{cekg} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cekg})) \wedge \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cekz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad ((\exp \mathit{cekz} = 1) \Leftrightarrow \exists \mathit{cekk} \in \mathbb{Z}.\; (\mathit{cekz} = (\mathit{cekk} \cdot \mathit{cekg}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-kernel-generator-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cekg} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cekg})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{cekz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad ((\exp \mathit{cekz} = 1) \Leftrightarrow \exists \mathit{cekk} \in \mathbb{Z}.\; (\mathit{cekz} = (\mathit{cekk} \cdot \mathit{cekg}))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{cekg} = ((2 \cdot \pi) \cdot +i)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-two-pi-i}}
\vnbstmt{(\exp ((2 \cdot \pi) \cdot +i) = 1)}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-i-pi}}
\vnbstmt{(\exp (+i \cdot \pi) = -1)}
%
\end{lem}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} UPDATED 2026-09-25 (batch 31-B, the user's decision on PI): PROVEN, cc-exp-one-iff: exp z = 1 iff z = k (2 pi i) for some integer k. PI is DEFINED (structure-library/cc-pi.scm) as the positive real p with kernel(exp) = ZZ (2 p i), i.e. the generator of the kernel in the upper half plane divided by 2i; existence (the kernel is a subgroup of i RR, discrete, non-trivial since cos has a zero in (0,2), hence cyclic) and uniqueness are proven before the IOTA is formed. The notes use pi without defining it. Nothing near: no complex exponential, no pi (the symbol pi occurs in THEOREMS.md only as a bound variable in pigeonhole-infinite), no trigonometric functions. The real fragment of the statement -- exp t = 1 for real t only when t = 0 -- follows from r-exp-strictly-increasing and r-exp-zero but is not itself installed.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.19}
\begin{prop}[{exp is a bijection on a horizontal strip}]\label{thm:cc-exp-bijection-strip}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-bijection-strip}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} (\lambda \mathit{cxsz} \in \{\mathit{cxsq} \in \mathbb{C} : ((-\pi \leq \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq})) \wedge (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq}) < \pi))\}.\; \\ \quad \exp \mathit{cxsz}) \\ \in\; \mathrm{Bij}(\{\mathit{cxsq} \in \mathbb{C} : ((-\pi \leq \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq})) \wedge (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq}) < \pi))\}, \operatorname{difference}(\mathbb{C}, \operatorname{singleton}(0))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-bijection-open-strip}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} (\lambda \mathit{cxsz} \in \{\mathit{cxsq} \in \mathbb{C} : ((-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq})) \wedge (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq}) < \pi))\}.\; \\ \quad \exp \mathit{cxsz}) \\ \in\; \mathrm{Bij}(\{\mathit{cxsq} \in \mathbb{C} : ((-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq})) \wedge (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsq}) < \pi))\}, \{\mathit{cxsu} \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) \leq 0))\}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-surjective-strip}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cxsw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg (\mathit{cxsw} = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{cxsz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (-\pi \leq \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsz})) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsz}) < \pi) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\exp \mathit{cxsz} = \mathit{cxsw}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-injective-strip}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cekz}, \mathit{cekw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (-\pi \leq \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cekz})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cekz}) < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (-\pi \leq \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cekw})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cekw}) < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\exp \mathit{cekz} = \exp \mathit{cekw}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{cekz} = \mathit{cekw}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-open-strip-onto}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cxsw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsw}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsw}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{cxsz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsz})) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsz}) < \pi) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\exp \mathit{cxsz} = \mathit{cxsw}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-open-strip-avoids-negatives}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cxsz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsz})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsz}) < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\exp \mathit{cxsz}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\exp \mathit{cxsz}) \leq 0)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-polar-form}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cxsw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg (\mathit{cxsw} = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{cxsr}, \mathit{cxsth} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{cxsr}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (-\pi \leq \mathit{cxsth}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{cxsth} < \pi) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{cxsw} = (\mathit{cxsr} \cdot \exp (+i \cdot \mathit{cxsth}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-real-is-r-exp}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{cxst} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (\exp \mathit{cxst} = \exp\left(\mathit{cxst}\right)) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} PROVEN 2026-09-26 (batch 34) as the notes state it: cc-exp-bijection-strip says the lambda z in S. exp z is in bijection(S, cc minus \{0\}) for S the SEP \{-pi $<$= Im $<$ pi\}; cc-exp-bijection-open-strip the same for the open strip onto cc minus (-inf, 0]. Surjectivity goes through the polar form (cc-polar-form, cc-circle-arg by the IVT on cos) and the bridge cc-exp-real-is-r-exp (exp restricted to RR is the real exponential R-EXP, via the derivative of log(exp t) - t). Earlier: UPDATED 2026-09-25 (batch 31-B): the INJECTIVITY half is PROVEN for the complex exponential on the strip -pi $<$= Im z $<$ pi (cc-exp-injective-strip, by Lemma 2.18); surjectivity onto CC minus 0 and the open-strip statement wait on the polar form (exp unbounded on RR, IVT for the modulus and the argument). Only the real restriction, and under the library's own definition of R-EXP as the inverse of the integral LOG rather than as a power series. r-exp-log and log-r-exp say that R-EXP and LOG are mutually inverse between RR and the positive reals, log-surjective and r-exp-pos give surjectivity onto (0, +inf), and log-injective-pos / r-exp-strictly-increasing give injectivity. Nothing about the strips S = \{-pi $<$= Im z $<$ pi\} or S' = \{-pi $<$ Im z $<$ pi\}, about C minus \{0\} or about C minus (-inf, 0]; there is no pi and no complex exponential to state them with.

\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.20}
\begin{lem}[{The logarithm series has radius 1}]\label{thm:cps-log-radius-one}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-log-radius-one}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{clhc}(0) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{clhj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{clhc}((\mathit{clhj} + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{clhj}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((\mathit{clhj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{clhc}) = 1) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-log-series}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{algc}(0) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{algj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{algc}((\mathit{algj} + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{algj}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((\mathit{algj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{algr} < 1) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{algr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{algr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{cpdz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 0, \mathit{algr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{algc}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{cpdz}, \mathit{cpsk}))))), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \mathit{algz}, \operatorname{recip}((1 + \mathit{algz}))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-log-radius}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{algc}(0) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{algj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{algc}((\mathit{algj} + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{algj}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((\mathit{algj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 \leq \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{algr} < 1) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{algr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{algc})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cps-log-radius-le-one}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{clhc}(0) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{clhj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{clhc}((\mathit{clhj} + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{clhj}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((\mathit{clhj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{clhr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (1 < \mathit{clhr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg (\mathit{clhr} < \operatorname{cps\text{-}radius}(\mathit{clhc})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-series-terms-small}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhf} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}converges}(\mathit{clhf}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{clhe}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{pos\text{-}rr}(\mathit{clhe}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \exists \mathit{clhn} \in \mathbb{N}. \forall \mathit{clhm} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{clhn} \leq \mathit{clhm}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{magnitude}(\operatorname{clhf}(\mathit{clhm})) \leq \mathit{clhe}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-geometric-alternating}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algg} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad \forall \mathit{algj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{algg}(\mathit{algj}) = \operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{algj})) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{magnitude}(\mathit{algz}) < 1) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}converges}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{algg}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{algz}, \mathit{cpsk})))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{algg}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}(\mathit{algz}, \mathit{cpsk})))) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{recip}((1 + \mathit{algz})) \end{array}}
%
\end{lem}
%
\begin{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} PROVEN 2026-09-27 (batches 38 and 38-B): cps-radius of the series is exactly 1 (cps-log-radius-one; the upper half through the new general lemma cc-series-terms-small, the terms of a convergent complex series tend to 0, and Bernoulli), and the derivative is recip(1 + z) on every B(0, r), r $<$ 1. Earlier: PARTIAL 2026-09-27 (batch 38): the series is formed (as a lambda inside the theorems), its radius is at least 1 (cps-log-radius) and its derivative is recip(1 + z) on every B(0, r), r $<$ 1 (cps-log-series, by 2.10 termwise and the alternating geometric series cc-geometric-alternating). The other half, radius at most 1, is batch 38-B's item (4). Earlier: Nothing near: no radius of convergence, and the series sum\_k (-1)\textasciicircum{}(k-1) z\textasciicircum{}k / k is nowhere formed. The library's derivative of the logarithm is log-deriv (is-diff-at of x |-$>$ log(x) at c $>$ 0 with value recip-star(c)), proved from the integral definition, not from a series.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.21}
\begin{prop}[{The logarithm series agrees with ln on (0,2)}]\label{thm:log0-is-ln}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{log0-is-ln}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{algc}(0) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{algj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{algc}((\mathit{algj} + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{algj}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((\mathit{algj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algt} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{algt}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{algt} < 2) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{algc}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{algt} - 1), \mathit{cpsk})))) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \log\left(\mathit{algt}\right) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{log0-exp}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{algc}(0) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{algj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{algc}((\mathit{algj} + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{algj}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((\mathit{algj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad (\mathit{algr} < 1) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, \mathit{algr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \exp \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; (\operatorname{algc}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{algz} - 1), \mathit{cpsk})))) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \mathit{algz} \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{log0-is-log-on-ball}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algc} \in (\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}). \\ \quad (\operatorname{algc}(0) = 0) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \forall \mathit{algj} \in \mathbb{N}. \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{algc}((\mathit{algj} + 1)) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\operatorname{power}(-1, \mathit{algj}) \cdot \operatorname{recip}((\mathit{algj} + 1))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad ((\mathit{algr} \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, \mathit{algr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left(\mathit{algz}\right) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; \operatorname{cc\text{-}series\text{-}limit}((\lambda \mathit{cpsk} \in \mathbb{N}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{algc}(\mathit{cpsk}) \cdot \operatorname{power}((\mathit{algz} - 1), \mathit{cpsk})))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic-near-one}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad ((\mathit{algr} \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, \mathit{algr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, \mathit{algr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left(\mathit{algz}\right))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} PROVEN 2026-09-27 (batch 38) in the notes' wording: log0-is-ln says the series (39) at a real t in (0, 2) equals LOG(t), by the notes' argument (equal derivatives, equal value at 1). Also exp(log0 z) = z on every B(1, r), r $<$ 1 (log0-exp), and log0 IS the principal logarithm CC-LOG on B(1, pi/(1+pi)) (log0-is-log-on-ball: the radius where |log0 z| $<$ pi keeps the value in the strip; the full B(1, 1) waits for the identity theorem 3.35). Earlier: Nothing near: the power series log\_0 z = sum\_\{k$>$=1\} (-1)\textasciicircum{}(k-1) (z-1)\textasciicircum{}k / k does not exist in the library. LOG itself is present and is exactly the notes' ln (log-unfold: LOG(x) = the oriented integral of 1/z from 1 to x, with log-one, log-mul, log-deriv, log-strictly-increasing proven), so only the series and its identification with LOG are missing.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.3.3.1}
\begin{defn}[{The principal branch of the logarithm}]\label{thm:cc-log-spec}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-spec}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right) \in \mathbb{C}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right)) < \pi) \wedge \\ \quad \quad (\exp \log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right) = \mathit{clgw}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-exp-log}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\exp \log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right) = \mathit{clgw}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-exp}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgz})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgz}) < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\log\left(\exp \mathit{clgz}\right) = \mathit{clgz}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-char}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgw}, \mathit{clgz} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgz})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgz}) < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\exp \mathit{clgz} = \mathit{clgw}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right) = \mathit{clgz}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-unique}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clga}, \mathit{clgb} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clga})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clga}) < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgb})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgb}) < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\exp \mathit{clga} = \exp \mathit{clgb}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\mathit{clga} = \mathit{clgb}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-real}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgt} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{clgt}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (\log\left(\mathit{clgt}\right) = \log\left(\mathit{clgt}\right)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-one}}
\vnbstmt{(\log\left(1\right) = 0)}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-polar}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgr}, \mathit{clgth} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{clgr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (-\pi < \mathit{clgth}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad (\mathit{clgth} < \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \log\left((\mathit{clgr} \cdot \exp (+i \cdot \mathit{clgth}))\right) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\log\left(\mathit{clgr}\right) + (+i \cdot \mathit{clgth})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgs} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{clgs}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{clgw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left((\mathit{clgs} \cdot \mathit{clgw})\right) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (\log\left(\mathit{clgs}\right) + \log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-in-slit}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clgw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clgw}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad (\log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right) \in \mathbb{C}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad (-\pi < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clgw}\right)) < \pi) \end{array}}
%
\end{defn}

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} DEFINED 2026-09-27 (batch 38): CC-LOG(w) is the IOTA of the z with -pi $<$ Im z $<$ pi and exp z = w, for w in the slit plane \{u in cc : not(Im u = 0 and Re u $<$= 0)\} (structure-library/analytic-log.scm); existence is cc-exp-open-strip-onto (batch 34), uniqueness cc-log-unique, the characterisation cc-log-spec by iota-d. Laws: exp(log w) = w, log(exp z) = z on the strip, log = LOG on the positive reals (through the bridge cc-exp-real-is-r-exp), log 1 = 0, the polar form (40) log(r exp(i th)) = LOG r + i th, log(s w) = LOG s + log w for real s $>$ 0.
%
\renewcommand{\thethm}{2.3.3.1-hol}
\begin{prop}[{log is holomorphic on C minus (-inf, 0]}]\label{thm:cc-log-holomorphic}
%
\leavevmode
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\{\mathit{cxsu} \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) \leq 0))\}, \\ \quad (\lambda \mathit{clhw} \in \{\mathit{cxsu} \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) \leq 0))\}.\; \\ \quad \quad \log\left(\mathit{clhw}\right))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-deriv}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhb} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhb}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhb}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{is\text{-}diff\text{-}on}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}normed\text{-}field}, \\ \quad \quad \quad \{\mathit{cxsu} \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) \leq 0))\}, \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{clhw} \in \{\mathit{cxsu} \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) \leq 0))\}.\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left(\mathit{clhw}\right)), \\ \quad \quad \quad \mathit{clhb}, \operatorname{recip}(\mathit{clhb})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic-at}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clha} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clha}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clha}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \exists \mathit{clhp} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{clhp}) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{clha}, \mathit{clhp}) \\ \quad \quad \quad \subseteq\; \{\mathit{cxsu} \in \mathbb{C} : \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{cxsu}) \leq 0))\} \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{clha}, \mathit{clhp}), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{clhx} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{clha}, \mathit{clhp}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left(\mathit{clhx}\right))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-im-near-one}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhd} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{clhd}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{clhr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{clhr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad ((\mathit{clhr} \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad ((\mathit{clhr} \cdot (1 + \mathit{clhd})) \leq \mathit{clhd}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \forall \mathit{clhz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, \mathit{clhr}). \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhz}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhz}) \leq 0)) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (-\mathit{clhd} < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhz}\right))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhz}\right)) < \mathit{clhd}) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-rotate}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhw})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \log\left((+i \cdot \mathit{clhw})\right) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\log\left(\mathit{clhw}\right) + (+i \cdot (1/2 \cdot \pi))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-rotate-neg}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhw})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \log\left((-+i \cdot \mathit{clhw})\right) \\ \quad \quad =\; (\log\left(\mathit{clhw}\right) - (+i \cdot (1/2 \cdot \pi))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-mul}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhu} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhu}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhu}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{clhv} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad \quad \quad \neg ((\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhv}) = 0) \wedge (\operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhv}) \leq 0)) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad -\pi \\ \quad \quad \quad <\; (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhu}\right)) + \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhv}\right))) \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhu}\right)) + \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhv}\right))) \\ \quad \quad \quad <\; \pi \Rightarrow \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left((\mathit{clhu} \cdot \mathit{clhv})\right) \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad =\; (\log\left(\mathit{clhu}\right) + \log\left(\mathit{clhv}\right)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-right-half}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clhw} \in \mathbb{C}. \\ \quad (0 < \operatorname{real\text{-}part}(\mathit{clhw})) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad (-(1/2 \cdot \pi) < \operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhw}\right))) \wedge \\ \quad \quad (\operatorname{imag\text{-}part}(\log\left(\mathit{clhw}\right)) < (1/2 \cdot \pi)) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-pi-gt-three}}
\vnbstmt{(3 < \pi)}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-cos-pos-half}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{clht} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (-(1/2 \cdot \pi) < \mathit{clht}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad ((\mathit{clht} < (1/2 \cdot \pi)) \Rightarrow (0 < \cos \mathit{clht})) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic-near-one}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad ((\mathit{algr} \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, \mathit{algr}), \\ \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, 1, \mathit{algr}).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left(\mathit{algz}\right))) \end{array}}
\vnbpart{\texttt{cc-log-holomorphic-scale}}
\vnbstmt{\begin{array}{@{}l@{}} \forall \mathit{algr} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad (0 < \mathit{algr}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad ((\mathit{algr} \cdot (1 + \pi)) \leq \pi) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \forall \mathit{algs} \in \mathbb{R}. \\ \quad \quad \quad (0 < \mathit{algs}) \Rightarrow  \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \operatorname{holomorphic\text{-}on}(\operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{algs}, (\mathit{algs} \cdot \mathit{algr})), \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad (\lambda \mathit{algz} \in \operatorname{ball}(\operatorname{cc\text{-}ms}, \mathit{algs}, (\mathit{algs} \cdot \mathit{algr})).\; \\ \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \log\left(\mathit{algz}\right))) \end{array}}
%
\end{prop}
%

\noindent\textbf{Deviation from the notes.} PROVEN 2026-09-27 (batch 38-B), with the derivative log'(w) = recip(w) (cc-log-deriv). THE ROUTE DIFFERS FROM THE NOTES: no sector cover and no numerical bound on pi is needed -- at every point a of the slit plane, log x = log a + log(x / a) on the ball B(a, |a| r) with r = (pi - |Im log a|) / (2 (1 + pi)), where log(x / a) is the power series near 1 (cc-log-holomorphic-at, cc-log-im-near-one). The notes' rotation laws log(i w) = log w + i pi/2 (cc-log-rotate, from cos $>$ 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2), cc-cos-pos-half) and pi $>$ 3 (cc-pi-gt-three, from cos(3/2) $>$ 0 by six terms of the series) are proven as well. Earlier: PARTIAL 2026-09-27 (batch 38): holomorphic on B(1, pi/(1+pi)) (as the power series log0) and on every scaled ball B(s, s pi/(1+pi)), s $>$ 0, by log(s w) = LOG s + log w. The rotation step log(i w) = log w + i pi/2 and the cover of the slit plane need cos $>$ 0 on (-pi/2, pi/2) and pi $>$ 3, which the tree lacked: batch 38-B.
